recipes.name: Chicken and Rice Taco Skillet

ingredients.name: Boneless, skinless chicken thighs
ingredients.prep: trimmed of excess fat and patted dry

ingredients.name: Kosher salt
ingredients.prep: 1 tsp for the chicken, ¼ tsp for the rice

ingredients.name: Taco seasoning
ingredients.prep: 2 tbsp for the chicken, 1 tbsp for the rice

ingredients.name: Lime
ingredients.prep: zest of ½ and 2 tbsp juice

ingredients.name: Cilantro
ingredients.prep: ¼ cup finely chopped leaves, plus more for garnish

instructions: Heat the oven to 350°F.
Pat the chicken dry and season it with the salt and 2 tablespoons of the taco seasoning.
In a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat, brown the chicken in the oil, about 3 minutes per side. It doesn't need to cook through. Set it aside.
Lower the heat to medium and cook the peppers, onion and garlic until tender, about 4 minutes.
Stir in the rice with a pinch of salt and the remaining tablespoon of taco seasoning. Toast for about 2 minutes.
Add the lime zest and juice, the broth and the cilantro, and bring to a simmer. Nestle the chicken back into the pan.
Cover and bake for 25 minutes, then uncover and bake 7 to 9 minutes more, until the rice is tender and the chicken is cooked through.
Fluff the rice with a fork and serve with guacamole, sour cream, chips and sliced jalapeño.

recipes.name: Beef Chili with Beans

ingredients.name: Kosher salt
ingredients.prep: 1 tsp for the vegetables, 1 tsp for the beef

ingredients.name: Hot sauce
ingredients.prep: such as Siete Traditional Hot Sauce

instructions: Heat the oil in a large Dutch oven over medium. Cook the onion, peppers, garlic and 1 teaspoon of the salt until soft, about 8 minutes.
Add the beef with the rest of the salt and the black pepper. Cook, breaking it up, until browned, about 7 minutes. Pour off all but 2 tablespoons of fat.
Stir in the tomato paste, hot sauce and spices and cook until fragrant, about 2 minutes. Add the tomatoes and broth and bring to a simmer.
Lower the heat, cover, and simmer for at least 30 minutes, stirring now and then. A few hours on low is even better.
About 15 minutes before serving, stir in the beans and the coconut sugar, if using, and cook uncovered until the beans are tender.
Serve with sour cream, cheddar, corn chips and sliced green onions.

recipes.name: One-Pan Italian Sausage and Orzo

ingredients.name: Yellow onion
ingredients.prep: finely diced (¾ cup, from about ½ medium onion)

instructions: Heat the oil in a large, deep skillet over medium. Brown the sliced sausage on all sides, 6 to 8 minutes, then set it aside.
Cook the onion and pepper in the same pan until soft, 2 to 3 minutes, scraping up the browned bits. Add the garlic for about a minute.
Stir in the orzo and toast for 1 to 2 minutes. Add the wine and let it mostly cook off.
Add the marinara, broth and seasonings. Simmer gently, uncovered, stirring now and then, about 12 minutes, until the orzo is tender and the sauce has thickened.
Stir in the cream, spinach, Parmesan and lemon juice until the spinach wilts. Season to taste.
Return the sausage to the pan to warm through. Top with torn basil and serve.

recipes.name: Turkey Taco Soup

ingredients.name: Yellow onion
ingredients.prep: finely diced (¾ cup, from about ½ large onion)

ingredients.name: Black pepper
ingredients.prep: freshly ground, plus more to taste

ingredients.name: Lime
ingredients.prep: zest of ½ and 2 tbsp freshly squeezed juice

instructions: Heat the oil in a large pot over medium-high. Cook the onion, pepper, jalapeño and garlic until soft, about 4 minutes.
Add the turkey and cook, breaking it up, until no longer pink, 6 to 8 minutes. Drain off any excess fat.
Stir in the salt, pepper, tomato paste and taco seasoning. Add the broth, tomatoes, green chiles, both beans and the lime zest, and bring to a simmer.
Lower the heat, cover, and cook about 10 minutes, until the beans are tender and the flavors blend.
Stir in the frozen corn, lime juice and cilantro and let it warm through. Season to taste.
Ladle into bowls and top with cheese, yogurt or sour cream, avocado and corn chips.

recipes.name: One-Pan Salmon with Herb Butter Couscous

ingredients.name: Salmon fillets
ingredients.prep: center-cut, 6 to 8 ounces each, skin removed

ingredients.name: Kosher salt
ingredients.prep: 1 tsp for the salmon, ½ tsp for the couscous, plus more to taste

ingredients.name: Black pepper
ingredients.prep: ground; ¼ tsp for the salmon, ¼ tsp for the couscous, plus more to taste

ingredients.name: Fresh thyme
ingredients.prep: 2 tsp leaves, plus more for garnish

ingredients.name: Lemon
ingredients.prep: zest of ½, plus 1 cut into wedges for serving

instructions: Season the tops of the salmon with a teaspoon of the salt and a pinch of pepper. Sear them seasoned side down in the oil in a large, deep skillet over medium-high until golden, about 3 minutes. Set aside. They finish cooking later.
Lower the heat to medium and cook the onion and garlic until tender, about 3 minutes. Add the couscous and toast, stirring, for 2 to 3 minutes.
Stir in the rosemary, thyme and parsley with the wine and cook until the wine is absorbed, about a minute.

Add the broth, lemon zest, onion powder, garlic powder and the rest of the salt and pepper. Bring to a quick simmer, then lower the heat, cover, and cook about 8 minutes until most of the liquid is absorbed.
Stir in the butter and Parmesan. Nestle the salmon, browned side up, into the couscous, cover, and cook 3 to 5 minutes more until cooked through.
Garnish with extra thyme and serve with lemon wedges.

recipes.name: Ginger and Peanut Butter Ground Turkey Stir-Fry
instructions: Whisk the peanut butter, coconut aminos, lime juice, sriracha, rice vinegar and sesame oil into a smooth sauce.
Heat the avocado oil in a large nonstick skillet over medium. Cook the shallot, garlic and ginger for about 2 minutes, watching that they don't burn.
Add the turkey, salt and pepper and cook, breaking it up, until no longer pink, about 7 minutes.
Pour in the sauce and add the green onions. Stir for about 3 more minutes, until the turkey is coated and the onions are just tender.
Serve over steamed rice, topped with mint, Thai basil and cilantro.

recipes.name: Shredded Beef Chipotle Burrito Bowls

ingredients.name: Boneless chuck roast
ingredients.prep: trimmed of excess fat and cut into 4 equal-sized chunks

ingredients.name: White rice, uncooked (for serving)
ingredients.prep: 4 cups prepared rice or cilantro rice

instructions: In the slow cooker, stir together the chipotles, vinegar, broth, salsa verde and garlic.
Season the roast all over with the salt, pepper, cumin and oregano. Nestle it into the sauce and add the bay leaves.
Cover and cook on low for 8 to 10 hours. For an Instant Pot, cook 60 minutes on high pressure, then release the pressure.
Move the roast to a sheet pan and shred it with two forks. Return it to the sauce, toss to coat, and let it rest at least 10 minutes.
Build the bowls with rice, then beef, then toppings such as corn, guacamole, pico de gallo, cilantro, hot sauce and a lime wedge.

recipes.name: Seared Chicken Thighs with Garlic-Ginger Broth and Rice

ingredients.name: Kosher salt
ingredients.prep: to taste, to season the chicken

ingredients.name: Fresh ginger (1-inch piece)
ingredients.prep: 1-inch knob, peeled and cut into thin matchsticks

ingredients.name: Baby bok choy
ingredients.prep: end removed so the leaves are separated

ingredients.name: White rice, uncooked (for serving)
ingredients.prep: serve over cooked rice, rice noodles, or miracle noodles

ingredients.name: Green onions
ingredients.prep: 2 scallions, very thinly sliced, to garnish

instructions: Heat the oil in a medium pot over medium-high. Season the thighs well with salt and pepper and sear 3 to 4 minutes per side, until golden and cooked through. Set them aside.
Lower the heat to medium-low. Cook the sesame oil, garlic and ginger for 1 to 2 minutes, stirring, without letting them burn.
Pour in the bone broth, scraping up the browned bits. Bring to a rapid simmer, then lower the heat, cover, and simmer gently for 5 to 10 minutes.
Whisk the coconut aminos, rice vinegar and tapioca flour into a slurry and stir it into the broth. Simmer until the broth is slightly thickened and silky.
Add the bok choy leaves and simmer about 3 minutes, until just wilted.
Put rice or noodles in two bowls, slice the chicken on top, and ladle over the bok choy and broth. Garnish with sliced green onions and chili crisp.

recipes.name: One-Pot Hamburger Helper

ingredients.name: Elbow pasta
ingredients.prep: dried, such as Jovial Brown Rice Pasta

instructions: Heat the oil in a large, deep skillet over medium-high. Cook the beef and onion with the garlic powder, paprika, salt, pepper and chili powder, breaking up the meat, until no longer pink, 5 to 7 minutes. Pour off all but 2 tablespoons of fat if needed.
Stir in the tomato paste.
Add the pasta, broth and milk. Bring to a boil, then simmer, stirring often, for 12 to 15 minutes, until the pasta is al dente and most of the liquid is absorbed.
Take the pan off the heat and fold in the cheese. Garnish with parsley and serve.

recipes.name: One-Pot Hamburger Helper Beef Stroganoff

ingredients.name: Button mushrooms
ingredients.prep: button (white), thinly sliced (2 cups); baby bella works too

ingredients.name: Fresh thyme
ingredients.prep: 2 to 3 sprigs, leaves only, for garnish

instructions: Heat the oil in a large skillet over medium-high. Cook the onion for 2 to 3 minutes, then add the beef with the garlic powder, onion powder, paprika, salt and pepper. Cook, breaking up the meat, until no longer pink, 5 to 7 minutes. Keep about 2 tablespoons of fat for the mushrooms and pour off the rest.
Stir in the mustard and mushrooms and cook until softened, 3 to 4 minutes.
Add the egg noodles, broth and vinegar. Bring to a boil and cook, stirring often, about 15 minutes, until the noodles are tender and the liquid is absorbed.
Take the pan off the heat and stir in the sour cream. Season with more salt if needed and garnish with thyme leaves.

recipes.name: One-Pot Spaghetti-O's with Mini Meatballs

ingredients.name: Kosher salt
ingredients.prep: 1 tsp for the meatballs, 1 tsp for the sauce

ingredients.name: Garlic
ingredients.prep: minced (2 cloves for the meatballs, 4 for the sauce)

ingredients.name: Fresh basil
ingredients.prep: 1 tbsp finely chopped for the meatballs, ¼ cup torn for the sauce, plus more for garnish

ingredients.name: Parmesan
ingredients.prep: grated (¼ cup for the meatballs, ½ cup for the sauce)

ingredients.name: Olive oil
ingredients.prep: extra virgin, plus more as needed

ingredients.name: Small pasta (ditalini, orzo, etc.)
ingredients.prep: such as anellini, ditalini, stellini, or orzo

instructions: Mix the beef, egg, salt, pepper, 2 cloves of the garlic, a tablespoon of chopped basil, the milk, a quarter cup of the Parmesan and the breadcrumbs by hand. Roll into half-inch meatballs.
Brown the meatballs in the oil in a large, deep skillet or braiser over medium-high, about 2 minutes per side, in batches. Set them aside. They don't need to cook through.

Lower the heat to medium-low. Cook the onion and the remaining garlic until tender, about 3 minutes. Add the marinara, broth, torn basil, parsley, coconut sugar, the rest of the Parmesan and the remaining salt. Simmer gently for 3 to 4 minutes.
Stir in the pasta and cook, stirring often, 8 to 10 minutes, until it's very al dente and has absorbed much of the sauce. It sticks easily, and it may need extra broth.
Return the meatballs and their juices and cook, stirring often, about 6 minutes more, until the meatballs are cooked through and the pasta is tender.
Cover and rest for 2 minutes. Garnish with basil and red pepper flakes.

recipes.name: Creamy One-Pot Lemon Feta Chicken with Orzo

ingredients.name: Kosher salt
ingredients.prep: 1 tsp in the spice blend, ½ tsp for the orzo

ingredients.name: Lemon
ingredients.prep: zest of ½ plus 2 tbsp juice, and wedges for serving

ingredients.name: Fresh oregano
ingredients.prep: 1 tbsp chopped leaves, plus more for serving

ingredients.name: Feta
ingredients.prep: crumbled, divided (½ cup in the orzo, ¼ cup on top)

instructions: Heat the oven to 375°F. Stir together the salt, turmeric, smoked paprika, pepper and cayenne.
Pat the chicken dry and season both sides generously with the spice blend. Brown it in the oil in a large, deep oven-safe skillet over medium-high, about 3 minutes per side, in batches. Set it aside.
Lower the heat to medium. Cook the shallot, garlic and red pepper flakes for 2 minutes. Add the Dijon and wine, scraping up the browned bits, and cook until reduced by half.

Stir in the orzo, broth, lemon zest and juice, a little more salt, the oregano, parsley and half a cup of the feta. Nestle the chicken back in and bake about 15 minutes, until the orzo is almost done.
Top with the remaining feta and bake about 5 minutes more, until the orzo is cooked and the feta has softened.
Garnish with more oregano and serve with lemon wedges.

recipes.name: Tie-Dye Chicken

ingredients.name: Boneless, skinless chicken breasts
ingredients.prep: 4 small, pounded to an even ½ inch and patted dry

instructions: Heat the oven to 400°F. Pound the chicken to an even half inch, pat it dry, season both sides with the salt, pepper and Italian seasoning, and dredge lightly in the flour.
Brown it in the oil in a large, deep oven-safe skillet over medium-high, about 3 minutes per side. It doesn't need to cook through.
Off the heat, spoon the marinara over and around the chicken, sprinkle on the mozzarella, and top with the pepperoni.
Bake on the top rack for 8 to 12 minutes, until the chicken is cooked through and the cheese is melted and lightly browned.
Let it cool for 3 to 5 minutes, then swirl or dollop the pesto on top. Garnish with basil.

recipes.name: Chipotle Sesame Adobo Steak Tacos

ingredients.name: Avocado oil
ingredients.prep: 3 tbsp for the sauce, 1 tbsp for the steak

ingredients.name: Flap, flank or skirt steak
ingredients.prep: cut into ½-inch cubes and patted dry

ingredients.name: Kosher salt
ingredients.prep: 1½ tsp for the steak, plus a pinch in the sauce

ingredients.name: Black pepper
ingredients.prep: freshly ground, plus a pinch in the sauce

ingredients.name: Flour tortillas
ingredients.prep: 8 to 10, such as Siete Almond Flour tortillas

instructions: Blend two of the chipotles with the sesame seeds, garlic, sesame oil, peanut butter, coconut sugar, 3 tablespoons of the avocado oil, vinegar, lime juice, tamari and a pinch of salt and pepper until smooth. Thin with a teaspoon or two of warm water if it's too thick.
Cut the steak into half-inch cubes and pat dry.
Heat the last tablespoon of avocado oil in a large skillet or griddle over medium-high. Cook the steak in a single layer, undisturbed, 3 to 4 minutes, until golden.
Sprinkle with the salt, pepper, cumin and paprika, toss, and cook 2 to 3 minutes more, until cooked through.
Lower the heat, add 2 tablespoons of the sauce, and toss to coat.
Warm the tortillas and fill them with steak. Drizzle with more sauce and top with avocado, cotija and cilantro.

recipes.name: Creamy Linguine with Lemon and Pancetta

ingredients.name: Kosher salt
ingredients.prep: a heavy pinch in the pasta water, a pinch in the sauce, more to taste

ingredients.name: Lemon
ingredients.prep: zest of ½ plus 2 tbsp juice (from about 1 small lemon)

instructions: Boil the linguine in well-salted water until al dente. Save about half a cup of the pasta water before draining.
Meanwhile, cook the pancetta in a large skillet over medium until the fat renders and it crisps, about 4 minutes.
Add the garlic, shallot and red pepper flakes and cook about 2 minutes without letting them burn.
Stir in the cream, lemon zest and pepper.

Add the drained pasta to the skillet with the pecorino, lemon juice and a pinch of salt. Toss with a quarter cup of the pasta water until the cheese melts and the pasta is glossy, adding more water if it's too thick.
Taste for salt and serve with extra pecorino and red pepper flakes.

recipes.name: Harissa Lamb Meatball Bowls

ingredients.name: Olive oil
ingredients.prep: extra virgin: 2 tbsp for the salad, plus a drizzle for the baking sheet

ingredients.name: Harissa sauce
ingredients.prep: such as Mina mild, plus more for serving

ingredients.name: Kosher salt
ingredients.prep: 1 tsp in the meatballs, ½ tsp in the salad, plus a pinch in the tahini sauce

ingredients.name: Cucumber
ingredients.prep: 2 cups quartered and thinly sliced (from about 1 cucumber)

ingredients.name: Red onion
ingredients.prep: ½ cup halved and thinly sliced

ingredients.name: Lemon
ingredients.prep: freshly squeezed: 2 tbsp for the salad, 1 tbsp for the tahini sauce

ingredients.name: Brown rice, uncooked (for serving)
ingredients.prep: serve over 2 cups cooked brown rice

instructions: Heat the oven to 400°F and lightly oil a small baking sheet.
Mix the lamb, egg, harissa, salt, curry powder, garlic powder, coriander, paprika and tapioca flour by hand. Roll into 1-inch balls (damp hands help) and set them on the pan.
Bake about 15 minutes, until golden and cooked through.
Meanwhile, toss the cucumber, tomatoes, red onion, olive oil, 2 tablespoons of the lemon juice, salt and pepper.
Stir together the tahini, yogurt, the remaining lemon juice, cilantro and a pinch of salt. Thin with 2 to 4 tablespoons of warm water until thick but drizzly.
Divide the rice among four bowls. Top with the meatballs, the salad, a spoonful of tahini sauce and an extra dab of harissa if you like. Garnish with dill.

recipes.name: Curried Turkey Sloppy Joes

ingredients.name: Red bell pepper
ingredients.prep: finely diced (½ cup, from about 1 bell pepper)

instructions: Heat the oil in a large skillet over medium. Cook the pepper, onion and garlic until they start to soften, 3 to 4 minutes.
Add the turkey, ginger, salt and pepper and cook, breaking the turkey into very small pieces, until no longer pink, 4 to 6 minutes. Drain off excess fat if needed.
Stir in the curry powder, garam masala, cumin and cayenne and toast for about 2 minutes.
Mix in the tomato paste, then the crushed tomatoes, broth and coconut sugar. Simmer, stirring often, about 4 minutes, until slightly thickened.
Lower the heat and stir in the yogurt until just combined. Season to taste.
Top with cilantro and spoon onto the buns, finishing with thin slices of serrano if you like.

recipes.name: Mongolian Chicken

ingredients.name: Boneless, skinless chicken breasts
ingredients.prep: pounded to an even ¼ inch, then sliced about 2 inches wide

ingredients.name: Avocado oil
ingredients.prep: 1 tsp for the chicken, 2 tbsp for the stir fry, plus more as needed

ingredients.name: Black pepper
ingredients.prep: white pepper is called for (black pepper is okay)

ingredients.name: Tapioca flour
ingredients.prep: arrowroot or tapioca: 1 tbsp for the chicken, 1 tbsp for the sauce

ingredients.name: Green onions
ingredients.prep: 8, white and light green parts sliced thin, dark green parts cut into 2-inch pieces

ingredients.name: Fresh ginger (1-inch piece)
ingredients.prep: 1-inch knob, peeled and cut into very thin matchsticks

ingredients.name: White rice, uncooked (for serving)
ingredients.prep: optional: serve as is or over prepared rice

instructions: Pound the chicken to an even quarter inch and slice it into thin strips about 2 inches wide. Toss with a teaspoon of avocado oil, the salt, pepper and a tablespoon of the tapioca flour.
Whisk the coconut aminos, fish sauce, sesame oil, rice vinegar, broth and the other tablespoon of tapioca flour into a sauce.

Heat 2 tablespoons of avocado oil in a large skillet or wok over medium-high. Brown the chicken in batches, so the pan isn't crowded, until golden and just cooked through, adding oil as needed. Set it aside.

Cook the white and light green parts of the green onions with the ginger and garlic for 20 to 30 seconds. Pour in the sauce, bring to a rapid simmer, and cook, stirring, until thickened, 2 to 3 minutes.
Return the chicken with the red pepper flakes and the dark green onion pieces and toss just until hot.
Serve right away, on its own or over rice.

recipes.name: Baked Salmon Sushi Bowls

ingredients.name: Avocado oil
ingredients.prep: 2 tbsp for the salmon, 2 tbsp for the dressing

ingredients.name: Coconut aminos
ingredients.prep: ¼ cup for the salmon, 2 tbsp for the dressing

instructions: Heat the oven to 325°F. Pat the salmon dry and put it in a small baking dish.

Whisk 2 tablespoons of the avocado oil with a quarter cup of the coconut aminos, the ginger and the sesame oil. Pour it over the salmon and sprinkle with the salt and pepper. Bake 25 to 30 minutes, until it flakes easily.
While it bakes, whisk the dressing: the remaining avocado oil, honey, the remaining coconut aminos, fish sauce, lemon juice, sriracha and garlic.
Flake the salmon into large pieces. Serve over rice with avocado, cucumber, green onions and nori. Drizzle with the dressing and sprinkle with sesame seeds.

recipes.name: Honey-Ginger Baked Salmon

ingredients.name: Toasted sesame seeds
ingredients.prep: 1 tsp in the sauce, 2 tsp for serving

ingredients.name: Green onions
ingredients.prep: 4 scallions, thinly sliced: white parts on the salmon, green parts for serving

instructions: Heat the oven to 400°F and set the salmon in an oven-safe baking dish.
Whisk the honey, coconut aminos, vinegar, garlic, ginger, a teaspoon of the sesame seeds and the sesame oil.
Pour the sauce over the salmon and top with the sliced white parts of the green onions, the salt and the pepper.
Bake 10 minutes, baste with the sauce, then bake 8 to 10 minutes more, until the salmon flakes easily.
Let it rest 5 minutes, spoon the sauce over the top, and garnish with the rest of the sesame seeds and the sliced green tops.

recipes.name: Spicy Cilantro Steak Bowls

ingredients.name: Flap, flank or skirt steak
ingredients.prep: 1 to 1½ lb flank steak, pricked all over with a fork

ingredients.name: Olive oil
ingredients.prep: ¼ cup in the marinade, ½ cup in the sauce

ingredients.name: Kosher salt
ingredients.prep: to taste on the steak, plus a pinch in the sauce

ingredients.name: Red onion (for pickled onions)
ingredients.prep: for quick pickled red onions (the page links a separate recipe)

instructions: Poke the steak all over with a fork, season both sides with salt and pepper, and marinate it in a zip bag with a quarter cup of the olive oil and the soy sauce, at least 30 minutes at room temperature or a few hours in the fridge. Take it out 30 minutes before cooking.
Blend the cilantro, jalapeño, garlic, half a cup of olive oil, red wine vinegar and a pinch of salt until smooth.
Grill or sear the steak over medium-high, about 5 minutes per side depending on thickness. Meanwhile, rub the corn with a little oil, season it, and grill 2 to 3 minutes per side.
Rest the steak under foil for a minute or so and cut the kernels off the cob.
Divide the greens, corn, avocado, pickled onions, tomatoes and cucumber among bowls.
Slice the steak very thinly against the grain, lay it on top, and drizzle everything with the cilantro sauce.

recipes.name: Whole30 Thai Basil Beef

ingredients.name: Flap, flank or skirt steak
ingredients.prep: flap or flank, pounded to ½ inch, then sliced very thin against the grain (halve long strips lengthwise)

ingredients.name: Avocado oil
ingredients.prep: avocado or olive oil: 1 tsp on the steak, 2 tbsp for searing

ingredients.name: Kosher salt
ingredients.prep: 1 tsp on the steak, ½ tsp with the vegetables

ingredients.name: Black pepper
ingredients.prep: freshly ground: ½ tsp on the steak, ¼ tsp with the vegetables

ingredients.name: Red bell pepper
ingredients.prep: large, seeds and core removed, very thinly sliced

ingredients.name: Thai chiles
ingredients.prep: 1 to 2, very thinly sliced (or ¼ tsp crushed red pepper flakes)

instructions: Pound the steak to about half an inch, then slice it against the grain into very thin strips, halving any long ones lengthwise.
Toss the strips with a teaspoon of the salt, half a teaspoon of pepper, a teaspoon of the oil and the tapioca flour.
Heat a skillet over high with the remaining 2 tablespoons of oil. Sear the steak 2 to 3 minutes per side, in batches, and set it aside.
Lower the heat to medium. Cook the onion, garlic, bell pepper and chiles with the rest of the salt and pepper until the onion is very tender, 5 to 7 minutes.
Return the beef with the coconut aminos and fish sauce and simmer 2 to 3 minutes, until thickened.
Off the heat, toss in the basil until just wilted. Serve right away with cauliflower rice, cilantro and lime wedges.

recipes.name: Chipotle Chicken Enchilada Bowls

ingredients.name: Chipotle enchilada sauce
ingredients.prep: 3 to 4 tbsp of homemade chipotle enchilada sauce (a separate recipe)

ingredients.name: Riced cauliflower
ingredients.prep: 4 cups (1 bag of Trader Joe's frozen cauliflower rice)

ingredients.name: Olive oil
ingredients.prep: 1 tbsp for the cauliflower, 1 tbsp for the chicken

instructions: For the cauliflower rice, heat a tablespoon of the oil over medium, cook the riced cauliflower about 2 minutes with salt and pepper, add the broth, lower the heat, cover, and steam about 4 minutes until the liquid is absorbed.
Heat the other tablespoon of oil over medium-high in a skillet, cast iron if you have it. Spread the chicken in a single layer and let it crisp on one side for about 2 minutes.
Add enchilada sauce to taste, toss to coat, and cook 2 minutes more. Add salt if needed.
Spoon the cauliflower rice into bowls, add the chicken, and arrange the radishes, spinach, guacamole and mango around it.
Garnish with cilantro and serve with lime wedges.

recipes.name: Spicy Chicken Tikka Tacos

ingredients.name: Yellow onion
ingredients.prep: diced small (1 cup, or ½ medium onion)

ingredients.name: Cayenne pepper
ingredients.prep: ¼ tsp for mild; omit if you don't like spice

ingredients.name: Flour tortillas
ingredients.prep: 8 to 10, such as Siete grain-free Cassava tortillas

ingredients.name: Cucumber
ingredients.prep: english cucumber (1 cup), cut in half lengthwise and sliced thin

instructions: Heat the oil in a large skillet over medium-high. Cook the onion, chicken, salt, pepper, garlic and ginger, breaking up the meat, until no longer pink, 5 to 7 minutes.
Add the curry powder, cayenne, cinnamon, paprika, cumin and turmeric and toast for about 2 minutes.
Stir in the tomato paste, then pour in the coconut milk and bring to a simmer.
Simmer, stirring now and then, 3 to 4 minutes, until slightly thickened. Taste and adjust the salt, pepper and cayenne.
Serve in warm tortillas with arugula, cucumber, cilantro, serrano and lime wedges.

recipes.name: Flap Steak Tacos with Jalapeño Chimichurri

ingredients.name: Avocado oil
ingredients.prep: 2 tbsp in the marinade, ⅓ cup in the chimichurri

ingredients.name: Lime
ingredients.prep: zest of ½ in the marinade, 2 tbsp freshly squeezed juice in the chimichurri, plus wedges for serving

ingredients.name: Kosher salt
ingredients.prep: 1½ tsp in the marinade, ½ tsp in the chimichurri (or more to taste)

ingredients.name: Black pepper
ingredients.prep: freshly ground: ½ tsp in the marinade, ½ tsp in the chimichurri

ingredients.name: Flap, flank or skirt steak
ingredients.prep: flap or skirt, sliced thinly against the grain after resting

ingredients.name: Jalapeño
ingredients.prep: large, seeds removed and roughly chopped

ingredients.name: Cilantro
ingredients.prep: 1 cup packed, roughly chopped leaves for the chimichurri, plus ¼ cup finely chopped for the tacos

instructions: Whisk 2 tablespoons of the avocado oil with the tamari, sesame oil, lime zest, cumin, garlic powder, chili powder, 1½ teaspoons salt and ½ teaspoon pepper. Add the steak and turn to coat. Marinate 20 minutes at room temperature, or refrigerate up to 24 hours (take it out 20 to 30 minutes before grilling).

Pulse the jalapeño, green onions, garlic, cilantro, the remaining avocado oil, 2 tablespoons lime juice, the red wine vinegar and the rest of the salt and pepper in a food processor until finely chopped but still a little textured. Adjust the seasoning.

Heat the grill to high. Let the extra marinade drip off the steak and grill 3 to 4 minutes per side for medium-rare. Rest 5 minutes, then slice thinly against the grain. A grill pan or cast iron works indoors.

Warm the tortillas on the grill grates, about 30 seconds per side. Stack two per taco and top with steak, avocado, diced white onion, cilantro and a generous drizzle of chimichurri. Serve with lime wedges.

recipes.name: Crockpot Creamy Coconut Chicken Tikka Masala

ingredients.name: Kosher salt
ingredients.prep: 1 tsp in the pot, plus more to taste

ingredients.name: Toasted sesame seeds
ingredients.prep: plain sesame seeds, for the chili butter

ingredients.name: Crushed red pepper flakes
ingredients.prep: chili flakes, 1 to 2 tsp (a pinch in the pot, the rest in the chili butter)

instructions: In the slow cooker, combine the chicken, yogurt, onion, shallot, garlic, ginger, garam masala, turmeric, a teaspoon of salt and a pinch of chili flakes. Let it sit 10 minutes.

Stir in the tomato paste and ⅓ cup of water. Cover and cook on low for 5 to 6 hours or on high for 3 to 4 hours. For an Instant Pot, cook 8 to 10 minutes at high pressure, release the steam, then switch to sauté for the next step.
Turn the heat to high, stir in the coconut milk, and cook uncovered about 10 minutes, until warmed. Stir in the cilantro.
Meanwhile, melt the butter with the sesame seeds, chili flakes and paprika and cook until the butter browns.
Serve the chicken and sauce over rice with naan, topped with the sesame chili butter.

recipes.name: Creamy Roasted Garlic Butternut Squash Pasta

ingredients.name: Garlic
ingredients.prep: 6 to 10 cloves (a halved whole bulb works too)

ingredients.name: Fresh rosemary
ingredients.prep: 2 tbsp chopped (1 tbsp on the squash, 1 tbsp in the butter)

ingredients.name: Kosher salt
ingredients.prep: to taste; the page gives no amount, so 1 tsp is an estimate

ingredients.name: Black pepper
ingredients.prep: to taste; the page gives no amount, so ½ tsp is an estimate

ingredients.name: Parmesan
ingredients.prep: grated (⅓ cup), plus more for serving

instructions: Heat the oven to 400°F. On a baking sheet, toss the squash and garlic with the olive oil, thyme, a tablespoon of the rosemary and a pinch each of red pepper flakes, salt and pepper. Lay the prosciutto around the squash. Bake 20 minutes, check the prosciutto, then bake 10 to 15 minutes more, until the squash is tender.
Purée the squash, the roasted garlic and the ricotta in a food processor until smooth. Season with salt and pepper.
Boil the pasta in salted water until al dente. Save a cup of the cooking water, then drain.

In a large skillet, melt the butter with the sage and the other tablespoon of rosemary until the butter starts to brown. Stir in the squash purée and half a cup of the pasta water, then melt in the gouda and Parmesan.
Add the pasta and toss, thinning with a little more pasta water if needed.
Divide among plates and top with extra Parmesan and the crispy prosciutto.

recipes.name: 30-Minute Spicy Indian Butter Chicken

ingredients.name: Boneless, skinless chicken thighs
ingredients.prep: breasts or thighs, cut into bite-size chunks

ingredients.name: Garlic
ingredients.prep: 6 cloves, minced or grated (half in the marinade, half in the sauce)

ingredients.name: Garam masala
ingredients.prep: 2 tsp for the chicken plus 1 tbsp for the sauce

ingredients.name: Ground cumin
ingredients.prep: 1 tsp for the chicken, 1 tsp for the sauce

ingredients.name: Turmeric
ingredients.prep: ½ tsp for the chicken, ½ tsp for the sauce

ingredients.name: Cayenne pepper
ingredients.prep: 1 to 2 tsp, to your taste (half in the marinade, half in the sauce)

ingredients.name: Kosher salt
ingredients.prep: 1 tsp on the chicken, plus more to taste

ingredients.name: Black pepper
ingredients.prep: to taste; the page gives no amount, so ½ tsp is an estimate

instructions: Toss the chicken with the yogurt, half the garlic and ginger, 2 teaspoons of the garam masala, a teaspoon of the cumin, ½ teaspoon of the turmeric, half the cayenne and a teaspoon of salt. Let it sit 5 to 10 minutes.
Heat the oil in a large skillet over medium-high. Sear the chicken on both sides, about 2 minutes, toss it with a tablespoon of butter, and set it aside.

Cook the onion in the same skillet for about 5 minutes. Add 2 tablespoons of butter, the rest of the garlic, ginger, garam masala, cumin, turmeric and cayenne, the red pepper flakes, and salt and pepper. Cook until very fragrant, about 5 minutes. Stir in the tomato paste and cook 3 to 4 minutes more.

Lower the heat. Add a cup of water and the coconut milk and simmer about 5 minutes, until slightly thickened. Stir in the last tablespoon of butter, and thin with a little more coconut milk if it's too thick.
Return the chicken and its juices and cook, stirring now and then, about 5 minutes, until the sauce thickens a little. Off the heat, stir in the cilantro and season to taste.
Serve over rice with naan.

recipes.name: Better Than Takeout Dan Dan Noodles

ingredients.name: Toasted sesame oil
ingredients.prep: ⅓ cup for the chili oil, plus 2 tbsp for browning the chicken

ingredients.name: Chinese egg noodles
ingredients.prep: Chinese-style egg noodles, or rice noodles (8 oz)

ingredients.name: Black pepper
ingredients.prep: to taste; the page gives no amount, so ¼ tsp is an estimate

instructions: Make the chili oil: warm a third of a cup of the sesame oil with the garlic and red pepper flakes in a large skillet over medium until the garlic is fragrant, about 5 minutes. Carefully pour it into a heatproof bowl or jar.
Stir together the soy sauce, hoisin, honey, vinegar, peanut butter and a third of a cup of water.
Cook the noodles as the package says, drain, and set aside. In the same pot, bring the broth and half the sauce to a simmer, stir in the spinach, and keep warm.

Heat the 2 remaining tablespoons of sesame oil in the empty skillet over medium-high. Brown the chicken with a little pepper, breaking it up, about 5 minutes. Add the mushrooms and shallot and cook 2 to 3 minutes. Pour in the rest of the sauce and simmer about 5 minutes, until it coats the meat and the edges crisp. Stir in 2 to 4 tablespoons of the chili oil.
Ladle the broth into bowls, add the noodles and toss. Top with the meat, more chili oil and green onions. Serve right away.

recipes.name: Skillet-Baked Ziti with Sausage and Ricotta

ingredients.name: Ziti or penne
ingredients.prep: gluten-free brown rice, or regular pasta (see note)

instructions: Put a rack in the center of the oven and heat it to 375°F.

Heat the oil in a large, deep oven-safe skillet or a 3.5-quart braiser with a lid over medium-high. Add the sausage and cook, breaking it up with a spoon, until it's cooked through and no longer pink, about 7 minutes.
Add the onion and garlic and cook until tender, about 4 minutes. Pour off the excess fat and put the sausage and vegetables back in the pan.

Lower the heat to medium-low. Stir in the Italian seasoning, salt, pepper, marinara, wine, broth, ricotta and Parmesan until well combined. Add the ziti and toss until it's coated, then spread everything in an even layer.
Tear the mozzarella into 1-inch pieces and scatter it over the top. Cover the skillet, move it to the oven, and bake 20 minutes.
Take off the lid and bake about 15 minutes more, until the mozzarella is bubbly and the pasta is tender.
Top with torn basil and let it cool slightly before serving. Leftovers keep up to 4 days in the fridge. Reheat in the microwave or a 350°F oven with a splash of broth.

Pasta note: regular pasta works. If you use gluten-free, the cookbook recommends brown rice pasta only, because it helps thicken the sauce. From your cookbook, Everyday Eats, page 105 (Pasta and Noodles).

recipes.name: Calabrian Carbonara

ingredients.name: Kosher salt
ingredients.prep: 1 tbsp for the pasta water, plus more to taste

ingredients.name: Pecorino Romano
ingredients.prep: freshly grated, plus more for serving

ingredients.name: Black pepper
ingredients.prep: coarsely ground, plus more for serving

ingredients.name: Calabrian peppers
ingredients.prep: jarred and chopped (1 to 2 tbsp; use 1 if you're heat-sensitive)

ingredients.name: Pancetta
ingredients.prep: or bacon, cut into small cubes

instructions: Bring a large pot of water to a boil. Add plenty of salt (about 1 tablespoon) and the pasta and cook until al dente, following the package.
Meanwhile, whisk the eggs, pecorino, black pepper and Calabrian peppers together in a medium bowl until well combined. Set aside.

Cook the pancetta in a large, deep skillet over medium heat, stirring now and then, until the fat renders and it starts to crisp, about 5 minutes. Turn the heat to low and keep it warm while the pasta finishes.
Drain the pasta and add it right away to the skillet with the pancetta, over low heat. Toss until combined.
Take the pan off the heat and pour in the egg mixture. Toss continuously for 2 to 3 minutes, so the eggs cook gently (don't let them scramble) and coat the pasta until it's glossy.
Taste and add salt if needed. Divide between two bowls and top with more pecorino and black pepper.
From your cookbook, Everyday Eats, page 106 (Pasta and Noodles).

recipes.name: One-Pot Cheesy Enchilada Helper
instructions: Heat the oil in a large, deep skillet over medium-high. Cook the onion and garlic, stirring, until the onion is tender, about 3 minutes.
Add the beef and cook, breaking it up with the edge of a spoon, until browned and cooked through, about 7 minutes. Drain off the excess fat and return the beef to the pan.
Stir in the salt, pepper, chili powder and cumin and cook until well combined and fragrant, about 2 minutes.

Add the pasta, enchilada sauce and broth. Stir, bring to a rapid simmer, then lower to a gentle simmer (about medium-low). Cook uncovered, stirring often, until the pasta is tender and most of the liquid is absorbed, 12 to 15 minutes.
Turn the heat to low. Stir in the yogurt, cheese and lime juice until the cheese melts and everything is combined. Off the heat, stir in the cilantro.
Leftovers keep up to 3 days in the fridge. Reheat with a splash of broth.
From your cookbook, Everyday Eats, page 109 (Pasta and Noodles).

recipes.name: Thai Red Curry Shrimp Noodles

ingredients.name: Kosher salt
ingredients.prep: 1 tbsp for the noodle water, 1½ tsp for the vegetables

ingredients.name: Lime
ingredients.prep: zest of ½, plus 2 tbsp freshly squeezed juice

ingredients.name: Shrimp
ingredients.prep: peeled, deveined, tail-off (36/40 count), patted dry

instructions: Bring a large pot of water to a boil. Add the rice noodles and plenty of salt (about 1 tablespoon) and cook until al dente, following the package. Drain, rinse under cold water, and set aside.
Heat the oil in a large, deep skillet over medium-high. Cook the bell pepper, onion, garlic, 1½ teaspoons salt and the black pepper, stirring, until the vegetables are tender, 3 to 4 minutes.
Add the curry paste and cook, stirring, until fragrant and toasted, about 2 minutes.
Pour in the coconut milk, coconut aminos, fish sauce, coconut sugar, lime zest and lime juice. Stir well, bring to a simmer, and cook, stirring often, until slightly thickened, 2 to 3 minutes.
Lower to a gentle simmer (about medium-low), add the shrimp and stir to coat. Cook until the shrimp are cooked through and no longer opaque, 3 to 4 minutes.
Rinse the noodles under cold water once more so they aren't sticky, then add them to the skillet with the cilantro and basil. Toss gently until the noodles are coated, about 2 minutes.
Serve with tongs, moving the noodles, shrimp and vegetables to bowls and pouring extra sauce on top.
From your cookbook, Everyday Eats, page 110 (Pasta and Noodles).

recipes.name: One-Pot Chicken Marsala Orzo

ingredients.name: Boneless, skinless chicken breasts
ingredients.prep: trimmed of excess fat, patted dry, cut into 1-inch pieces

ingredients.name: Kosher salt
ingredients.prep: 1 tsp on the chicken, 1 tsp with the garlic

ingredients.name: Olive oil
ingredients.prep: extra-virgin: 2 tbsp for the chicken, 1 tbsp for the mushrooms

ingredients.name: Shallot
ingredients.prep: large, halved and thinly sliced (¼ cup)

ingredients.name: Fresh thyme
ingredients.prep: 2 tsp leaves, plus more for serving

ingredients.name: Orzo
ingredients.prep: or brown rice orzo / another small pasta for gluten-free

ingredients.name: Lemon
ingredients.prep: zest of ½, plus 1 tbsp juice (about ½ lemon)

instructions: Toss the chicken with 1 teaspoon of the salt, the pepper, onion powder and dried thyme in a medium bowl.

Heat 2 tablespoons of the oil in a large, deep skillet or a 3.5-quart braiser with a lid over medium-high. Cook the chicken in a single layer, 3 to 4 minutes per side, until cooked through. Move it to a clean plate.

In the same pan, melt the remaining tablespoon of oil with the butter. Add the mushrooms and shallot and cook undisturbed for 5 minutes to get a good sear, then stir for 2 to 3 minutes more, until deep golden brown.

Lower the heat to medium. Add the garlic, the remaining teaspoon of salt and the fresh thyme and cook 1 minute, until fragrant. Add the marsala, scraping up the browned bits, and cook until reduced by half, about 1 minute.

Add the orzo, broth and lemon zest and stir. Bring to a rapid simmer, then lower to a gentle simmer (about medium-low) and cook 8 minutes, stirring often, until most of the liquid is absorbed and the orzo is almost done.
Turn the heat to low and add the chicken and its juices, the lemon juice and the crème fraîche. Stir until combined, cover, and cook until the orzo is al dente, 2 to 3 more minutes.
Scoop into bowls and garnish with extra thyme. Leftovers keep up to 3 days in the fridge. Reheat with a splash of broth.
From your cookbook, Everyday Eats, page 113 (Pasta and Noodles).

recipes.name: Sausage, Fennel, and Lemon Pasta

ingredients.name: Kosher salt
ingredients.prep: 1 tbsp for the pasta water, 1 tsp in the sauce

ingredients.name: Mezze maniche or rigatoni
ingredients.prep: or brown rice pasta for gluten-free

ingredients.name: Lemon
ingredients.prep: zest of ½, plus 2 tbsp freshly squeezed juice (about 1 lemon)

instructions: Bring a large pot of water to a boil. Add plenty of salt (about 1 tablespoon) and the pasta and cook until al dente. Save 1 cup of the starchy pasta water, then drain the pasta and set it aside.

While the pasta cooks, heat the oil in a large, deep skillet over medium-high. Cook the sausage, breaking it up with the edge of a spoon, until cooked through and no longer pink, about 7 minutes. Drain off the excess fat and return the sausage to the pan.

Add the shallot and cook until softened, about 3 minutes. Stir in the kale, garlic, fennel seeds and pepper flakes and cook 1 to 2 minutes, stirring now and then, until the garlic is fragrant and the kale has wilted.
Pour in the wine (or broth) and cook, scraping up the browned bits, until reduced by half, about 2 minutes. Stir in ½ cup of the reserved pasta water, the lemon zest and the lemon juice.
Turn the heat to low and add the yogurt, Parmesan, 1 teaspoon salt and the pepper. Stir until creamy and smooth, and don't let it boil or the yogurt will curdle.
Add the cooked pasta and toss to coat. If the sauce is too thick, add more pasta water ¼ cup at a time. Stir in the parsley.
Serve right away with extra Parmesan and pepper flakes on top.
From your cookbook, Everyday Eats, page 114 (Pasta and Noodles).

recipes.name: Golden Curry Veggie Udon Noodles

ingredients.name: Red bell pepper
ingredients.prep: medium, seeded and sliced into ¼-inch-wide strips

ingredients.name: Green onions
ingredients.prep: 4, thinly sliced, white and green parts kept separate

ingredients.name: Kosher salt
ingredients.prep: 1 tsp in the skillet, 1 tbsp in the noodle water, plus more to taste

ingredients.name: Lime
ingredients.prep: 2 tbsp freshly squeezed juice (about 1 lime), plus wedges for serving

instructions: Bring a medium pot of water to a boil.

Meanwhile, heat the oil in a large, deep skillet over medium-high. Cook the broccoli, bell pepper, carrots, the white parts of the green onions, ginger, garlic, black pepper and 1 teaspoon salt, stirring, until the vegetables begin to soften, about 4 minutes.
Lower the heat to medium and add the curry powder, turmeric and pepper flakes. Cook, stirring, until fragrant, about 1 minute.
Add the coconut aminos, fish sauce and coconut milk and bring to a rapid simmer. Turn the heat to low so the sauce simmers very lightly while the noodles cook.
Add the udon and plenty of salt (about 1 tablespoon) to the boiling water and cook as the package says. Save ½ cup of the water, then drain the noodles.

Add the noodles to the sauce with the green parts of the green onions, the lime juice and the basil. Toss until coated, adding the saved water ¼ cup at a time if they seem dry, until glossy. Taste and adjust the salt.
Divide among four bowls and top with the peanuts. Serve with lime wedges.
From your cookbook, Everyday Eats, page 117 (Pasta and Noodles).

recipes.name: One-Skillet Buffalo Chicken Pasta

ingredients.name: Avocado oil
ingredients.prep: 2 tbsp for the pasta, 1 tbsp for the topping

ingredients.name: Green onions
ingredients.prep: 4, thinly sliced, white and green parts kept separate

ingredients.name: Kosher salt
ingredients.prep: 1½ tsp in the pasta, ¼ tsp in the topping

ingredients.name: Shredded sharp cheddar
ingredients.prep: ¾ cup in the pasta, ¼ cup on top

ingredients.name: Fresh parsley
ingredients.prep: 1 tbsp finely chopped leaves, for serving

instructions: Put a rack in the middle of the oven and heat it to 400°F.

Heat 2 tablespoons of the oil in a large, deep oven-safe skillet or 3.5-quart braiser over medium-high. Cook the white parts of the green onions and the garlic, stirring, until softened, about 3 minutes.

Add the pasta, broth, 1½ teaspoons salt, the pepper, garlic powder and paprika. Bring to a rapid simmer, then turn to medium for a steady bubble (not a hard boil). Cook, stirring often, until the pasta is tender and most of the broth is absorbed, with a little liquid left, 13 to 15 minutes.

Turn the heat to low and stir in the Buffalo sauce, yogurt and the pasta's share of the cheddar until combined and just melted. Off the heat, stir in the chicken, the green parts of the green onions and the blue cheese, then spread it in an even layer.
For the topping, mix the panko, the remaining tablespoon of oil and ¼ teaspoon salt until the crumbs are coated.
Sprinkle the remaining cheddar over the pasta, then the panko mixture. Bake until the cheese is bubbly and the crumbs are golden, 6 to 7 minutes.
Let it cool slightly, then garnish with parsley. Leftovers keep up to 3 days in the fridge. Reheat with a splash of broth.
From your cookbook, Everyday Eats, page 118 (Pasta and Noodles).

recipes.name: Pesto Unstuffed Shells

ingredients.name: Olive oil
ingredients.prep: extra-virgin: 2 tbsp for the bread crumbs, plus a little to grease the baking dish

ingredients.name: Fresh basil
ingredients.prep: ½ cup julienned leaves, plus more for serving

ingredients.name: Lemon
ingredients.prep: zest of ½, plus 2 tbsp juice (about 1 lemon)

ingredients.name: Kosher salt
ingredients.prep: ½ tsp in the ricotta, ¼ tsp in the crumbs, about 1 tbsp in the pasta water

ingredients.name: Parmesan
ingredients.prep: freshly grated: ¼ cup in the ricotta, ½ cup on top

instructions: Put a rack in the middle of the oven and heat it to 375°F. Grease a 9×13-inch baking dish with oil and set it aside.
Ricotta mixture: stir together the ricotta, garlic, basil, lemon zest and juice, ½ teaspoon salt, the pepper and ¼ cup of the Parmesan. Keep it in the fridge.
Bread crumbs: mix the panko, the 2 tablespoons oil, ¼ teaspoon salt, the oregano and the paprika until the panko is evenly coated.
Boil the shells in a large pot of well-salted water (about 1 tablespoon salt) until al dente. Save 1 cup of the pasta water, then drain and return the shells to the pot.
Stir in the pesto, ¼ cup of the pasta water and half of the ricotta mixture until the shells are coated and the sauce is smooth and glossy, adding more pasta water ¼ cup at a time if needed.

Pour the pasta into the baking dish in an even layer. Dollop the rest of the ricotta mixture on top, then add the mozzarella and the remaining ½ cup Parmesan, and scatter the bread crumbs over everything.

Bake about 20 minutes, until bubbly with a golden top. Let it stand 5 minutes, then top with more basil and the pine nuts. To toast pine nuts, stir them in a dry skillet over medium heat until golden and fragrant, 3 to 5 minutes, and watch them closely.

Make ahead: bake, cool, and refrigerate covered up to 3 days; reheat covered with foil at 350°F about 30 minutes. It also freezes up to 2 months (wrap tightly, thaw overnight, bake as directed). From your cookbook, Everyday Eats, page 121 (Pasta and Noodles).

recipes.name: Tipsy Noodles

ingredients.name: Thai chiles
ingredients.prep: 1 to 3, minced (3 for spicy, 2 medium, 1 mild; or about ½ serrano)

ingredients.name: Kosher salt
ingredients.prep: about 1 tbsp for the noodle water

ingredients.name: Fresh Thai or regular basil
ingredients.prep: 1 cup packed leaves, plus more for garnish

instructions: Bring a large pot of water to a boil.
Meanwhile, whisk the coconut aminos, vinegar, fish sauce, sesame oil, coconut sugar, garlic, ginger, Thai chiles, broth and tapioca flour in a small bowl. Set aside.
Heat the avocado oil in a large, deep skillet over medium-high. Cook the beef, breaking it up, until no longer pink, about 7 minutes. Drain off the excess fat and return the beef to the pan.
Add the bell pepper, green onions and carrots and cook, stirring, until they begin to soften, 3 to 4 minutes.
Lower the heat to medium and pour in the sauce. Bring to a simmer and cook, stirring often, until it thickens a bit, about 4 minutes. Turn the heat to low to keep it warm.
Cook the rice noodles in the boiling water with plenty of salt (about 1 tablespoon), as the package says (usually 2 to 6 minutes). Drain and rinse under cold water.
Add the noodles to the skillet and toss until glossy and coated, about 2 minutes. Add the lime juice and basil and toss until the basil just wilts, 1 more minute.
Divide among four bowls with more basil on top. Leftovers keep 3 to 4 days in the fridge. From your cookbook, Everyday Eats, page 122 (Pasta and Noodles).

recipes.name: One-Pot Italian Shells and Cheese
instructions: Heat the oil in a large, deep-sided skillet or pot over medium-high. When it shimmers, cook the onion and garlic, stirring now and then, until just softened, about 2 minutes.
Add the sausage and cook, breaking it up, until cooked through and no longer pink, about 7 minutes. Drain all but 2 tablespoons of fat and return the sausage to the pan.
Stir in the salt, pepper and oregano, then the tomato paste until it's well mixed with the sausage.

Add the pasta, broth, tomato sauce and vinegar and stir. Bring to a boil, then lower to a gentle simmer (about medium-low). Cook, stirring often, until most of the liquid is absorbed and the pasta is al dente, 13 to 15 minutes.
Turn the heat to low and stir in the mozzarella until melted. Taste and add salt if needed.
Top with basil and parsley. Leftovers keep up to 3 days in the fridge. From your cookbook, Everyday Eats (Pasta and Noodles).

recipes.name: Oven-Roasted Shrimp Scampi

ingredients.name: Shallot
ingredients.prep: large, halved and thinly sliced (½ cup)

ingredients.name: Lemon
ingredients.prep: zest of ½, plus wedges for serving

ingredients.name: Kosher salt
ingredients.prep: 1 tsp in the dish, about 1 tbsp in the pasta water, plus more to taste

ingredients.name: Shrimp
ingredients.prep: peeled, deveined, tail-off (31/40 count), patted dry

instructions: Heat the oven to 375°F and bring a large pot of water to a boil.
In a 9×13-inch baking dish, toss together the garlic, shallot, pepper flakes, oil, wine, lemon zest, 1 teaspoon salt, the black pepper and the shrimp. Spread into an even layer.
Bake until the shrimp are pink and cooked through, about 13 minutes.
Meanwhile, add plenty of salt (about 1 tablespoon) and the pasta to the boiling water and cook as the package says.
Drain the pasta, add it to the baking dish and gently toss until coated. Add the Parmesan (if using) and parsley and toss once more. Taste and add salt if needed.
Divide among four bowls and serve with lemon wedges. Leftovers keep up to 3 days in the fridge. From your cookbook, Everyday Eats, page 126 (Pasta and Noodles).

recipes.name: Chicken and Broccoli Stir-Fry

ingredients.name: Boneless, skinless chicken breasts
ingredients.prep: trimmed of excess fat, patted dry, pounded to ½ inch and cut into 1-inch pieces

ingredients.name: Tapioca flour
ingredients.prep: 2 tbsp on the chicken, 1 tbsp in the sauce

ingredients.name: Coconut aminos
ingredients.prep: 1 tbsp on the chicken, ⅓ cup in the sauce

instructions: Cover the chicken breasts with parchment or plastic wrap and pound to an even ½-inch thickness. Cut into 1-inch pieces.
Toss the chicken with the salt, pepper, 2 tablespoons tapioca flour, 1 tablespoon coconut aminos and the baking soda in a medium bowl. Set aside.
Sauce: whisk the remaining coconut aminos (⅓ cup), sesame oil, fish sauce, broth, garlic, ginger, pepper flakes (if using) and 1 tablespoon tapioca flour in a small bowl.

Heat the avocado oil in a large, deep nonstick skillet over medium-high. Working in batches, cook the chicken in a single layer, undisturbed, until a golden-brown crust forms, about 3 minutes, then flip and cook about 3 minutes more. Move it to a clean plate.
Lower the heat to medium. Add the broccoli and ¼ cup water, scraping up the browned bits, and cook until the broccoli is bright green and the water has evaporated, about 3 minutes.

Return the chicken and its juices to the skillet and pour in the sauce. Simmer, stirring now and then, until the sauce thickens and coats the chicken, about 3 minutes. Take it off the heat, let it cool slightly, and serve over cauliflower rice or steamed rice.
Leftovers keep 3 to 4 days in the fridge. Reheat gently in a skillet over medium heat with a splash of broth. From your cookbook, Everyday Eats.

recipes.name: Sheet Pan Chicken with Soppressata and Peppers

ingredients.name: Lemon
ingredients.prep: zest of ½, plus 2 tbsp juice (about 1 lemon)

ingredients.name: Fresh oregano
ingredients.prep: 2 tbsp roughly chopped leaves, divided (1 tbsp in the mixture, 1 tbsp on top)

ingredients.name: Bone-in, skin-on chicken thighs
ingredients.prep: trimmed of excess fat and patted dry

ingredients.name: Red onion
ingredients.prep: small, halved and thinly sliced (½ cup)

ingredients.name: Soppressata or salami
ingredients.prep: hard, casings removed, cut into small dice (about ¾ cup)

instructions: Heat the oven to 425°F and line a sheet pan with parchment paper.
In a small bowl, whisk the oil, mustard, garlic, lemon zest and juice, 1 tablespoon of the oregano, the salt, black pepper, paprika and pepper flakes.

Put the chicken thighs on the pan and scatter the bell peppers, onion and soppressata around them. Pour the mustard mixture over everything and toss, massaging it into the chicken. Spread it into a single layer with the thighs skin side up.
Bake until the chicken is cooked through and golden, 30 to 40 minutes, tossing the vegetables halfway through.
Let it cool slightly, then top with the olives. Divide among four plates and finish with the goat cheese (if using), the remaining tablespoon of oregano and the mint.
Leftovers keep up to 3 days in the fridge (keep the goat cheese and herbs separate). From your cookbook, Everyday Eats, page 132 (Poultry).

recipes.name: Creamy One-Pot Lemon Feta Chicken with Orzo (cookbook)

ingredients.name: Kosher salt
ingredients.prep: 1 tsp on the chicken, ½ tsp in the orzo

ingredients.name: Boneless, skinless chicken breasts
ingredients.prep: trimmed of excess fat and patted dry

ingredients.name: Shallot
ingredients.prep: large, halved lengthwise and thinly sliced (½ cup)

ingredients.name: Lemon
ingredients.prep: zest of ½ plus 2 tbsp juice (about 1 lemon), and wedges for serving

ingredients.name: Fresh oregano
ingredients.prep: 1 tbsp chopped leaves, plus more for serving

ingredients.name: Feta
ingredients.prep: crumbled, divided (½ cup in the orzo, ¼ cup on top)

instructions: Heat the oven to 375°F. Mix the salt, pepper, turmeric, paprika and cayenne in a small bowl.

Season both sides of the chicken breasts generously with the spice blend. Heat the oil in a large, deep oven-safe skillet or 3.5-quart braiser over medium-high and brown the chicken, about 3 minutes per side. It won't be cooked through yet. Move it to a clean plate.

In the same skillet, lower the heat to medium and cook the shallot, garlic and pepper flakes for 2 minutes. Stir in the mustard and wine, scraping up the browned bits, and cook until the wine has reduced by half, about 2 minutes.
Add the orzo, broth, lemon zest and juice, ½ teaspoon salt, the oregano, parsley and ½ cup of the feta. Stir, then nestle the chicken and its juices into the skillet.

Bake uncovered about 15 minutes, until the chicken is cooked and the orzo is almost done. Top with the remaining ¼ cup feta and bake 5 more minutes, until the orzo is cooked and the feta has softened.
Garnish with more oregano and serve with lemon wedges. This is the cookbook's version of the blog recipe, made with chicken breasts. From your cookbook, Everyday Eats (Poultry).

recipes.name: Larb Gai-Inspired Lettuce Wraps

ingredients.name: Shallot
ingredients.prep: large, halved and thinly sliced (1 cup)

ingredients.name: Thai chiles
ingredients.prep: 1 to 3, minced (see the Tipsy Noodles note for heat)

ingredients.name: Lime
ingredients.prep: ¼ cup freshly squeezed juice (about 2 limes), plus wedges for serving

ingredients.name: Cilantro
ingredients.prep: ½ cup finely chopped leaves, plus more for garnish

ingredients.name: Fresh mint
ingredients.prep: ¼ cup finely chopped leaves, plus more for garnish

ingredients.name: Persian cucumbers
ingredients.prep: thinly sliced on the diagonal (about 2 cups)

instructions: Toast the cashews and sesame seeds in a large, dry skillet over medium-high until golden and fragrant, about 2 minutes, watching so they don't burn. Move to a bowl.
Turn the heat to medium-high, add the oil and cook the shallot until slightly tender, about 2 minutes.
Add the chicken, salt, pepper, garlic and Thai chiles. Cook, breaking up the meat, until cooked through and no longer pink, about 7 minutes.

Lower the heat to medium-low. Add the coconut aminos, lime juice, coconut sugar, fish sauce and three-quarters of the cashew-sesame mixture (save the rest for serving). Cook, stirring, about 4 minutes. Off the heat, stir in the cilantro and mint.
Spoon the mixture into lettuce cups, top with cucumber slices and the rest of the cashew-sesame mixture, and garnish with more cilantro and mint. Serve with lime wedges.
Keep leftover filling, lettuce, cucumbers and topping separate in the fridge for up to 3 days. From your cookbook, Everyday Eats, page 136 (Poultry).

recipes.name: Roasted Buffalo Chicken Thighs with Brussels Sprouts

ingredients.name: Bone-in, skin-on chicken thighs
ingredients.prep: large, trimmed of excess fat and patted dry

ingredients.name: Kosher salt
ingredients.prep: 1 tsp on the chicken, ½ tsp with the Brussels sprouts

ingredients.name: Red onion
ingredients.prep: small, halved and thinly sliced (1 cup)

ingredients.name: Blue cheese
ingredients.prep: crumbled, ⅓ cup (omit for dairy-free and paleo)

instructions: Heat the oven to 400°F. Season both sides of the chicken with 1 teaspoon of the salt, the pepper, onion powder and garlic powder.

Heat the oil in a large, deep oven-safe skillet or 3.5-quart braiser over medium-high. Cook the thighs skin side down, undisturbed, until a golden-brown crust forms and they lift easily, about 4 minutes. They won't be cooked through yet. Move them to a clean plate.

Lower the heat to medium-low. Add the Brussels sprouts, onion, the remaining ½ teaspoon salt and the lemon juice, scraping up the browned bits, and cook until the juice has reduced by half, 1 to 2 minutes. Spread the sprouts into an even layer and take the pan off the heat.
Set the thighs skin side up on top. Roast uncovered about 25 minutes, until the chicken is almost cooked through and the sprouts are lightly browned.

Carefully take the skillet out, toss the sprouts, and spoon 1 tablespoon of Buffalo sauce over each thigh, spreading it over the tops. Roast 5 to 8 more minutes, until the sauce caramelizes and the chicken is cooked through, watching that it doesn't burn.
Finish with the blue cheese (if using), dill and chives. The skin won't stay crisp in leftovers (3 days in the fridge). From your cookbook, Everyday Eats, page 141 (Poultry).

recipes.name: Saucy Chipotle Chicken Tacos

ingredients.name: Avocado oil
ingredients.prep: 1 tbsp for the slaw, 2 tbsp for the chicken, plus a little to warm the tortillas

ingredients.name: Kosher salt
ingredients.prep: ½ tsp in the slaw, 1 tsp on the chicken

ingredients.name: Ground cumin
ingredients.prep: ½ tsp in the slaw, ½ tsp on the chicken

ingredients.name: Lime
ingredients.prep: 2 tbsp freshly squeezed juice (about 1 lime) for the slaw, plus wedges for serving

ingredients.name: Boneless, skinless chicken thighs
ingredients.prep: trimmed of excess fat, patted dry, cut into ½-inch pieces

ingredients.name: Chipotle chiles in adobo
ingredients.prep: 1 pepper, finely minced, plus 1 tbsp of the sauce

ingredients.name: Corn tortillas
ingredients.prep: or almond flour tortillas for grain-free

instructions: Slaw: toss the cabbage with the oil, salt, ½ teaspoon cumin and the lime juice in a large bowl. Set aside.

Heat 2 tablespoons oil in a large nonstick skillet over medium-high. Add the chicken in a single layer and season with the salt, pepper, paprika, oregano and ½ teaspoon cumin. Cook, tossing now and then, until golden brown on all sides, 4 to 5 minutes.
Lower the heat to medium and stir in the garlic, tomato paste, minced chipotle and the tablespoon of adobo sauce until fragrant, about 2 minutes.
Pour in the broth, vinegar and honey, scraping up the browned bits. Bring to a simmer and cook until the sauce reduces slightly, 3 to 4 minutes, then turn the heat to low.
Warm the tortillas one at a time in a small skillet with ½ teaspoon oil, about 30 seconds per side, or char them over a gas flame.
Fill the tortillas with the chicken, top with slaw, a drizzle of salsa verde, white onion and cilantro, and serve with lime wedges.
Keep the chicken, slaw, tortillas and toppings separate in the fridge for up to 3 days. From your cookbook, Everyday Eats, page 142 (Poultry).

recipes.name: Skillet French Onion Chicken with Mushrooms

ingredients.name: Boneless, skinless chicken breasts
ingredients.prep: small, trimmed of excess fat, patted dry, and pounded to ½ inch

ingredients.name: Kosher salt
ingredients.prep: 1 tsp on the chicken, ½ tsp with the onions

ingredients.name: Olive oil
ingredients.prep: extra-virgin: 2 tbsp for the chicken, 1 tbsp for the onions

ingredients.name: Yellow onion
ingredients.prep: small, halved and thinly sliced (about 1 cup)

instructions: Heat the oven to 375°F. Cover the chicken breasts with parchment or plastic wrap and pound to an even ½-inch thickness. Season both sides with 1 teaspoon of the salt, the pepper and the paprika.
Dredge each piece in the flour until coated on both sides, shaking off the excess.

Heat 2 tablespoons oil in a large oven-safe skillet or 3.5-quart braiser over medium-high. Working in batches, brown the chicken 2 to 3 minutes per side. It won't be cooked through yet. Move it to a clean plate.
Lower the heat to medium. Add the remaining tablespoon of oil, the onion, mushrooms, garlic and remaining ½ teaspoon salt and cook, stirring, until tender, 5 to 7 minutes.
Stir in the mustard, coconut aminos and thyme, then add the wine and broth, stirring until combined.
Nestle the chicken and its juices back into the skillet and top with the Gruyère. Bake uncovered until the chicken is cooked through and the cheese is browned and bubbly, about 12 minutes.
Leftovers keep up to 3 days in the fridge. From your cookbook, Everyday Eats, page 145 (Poultry).

recipes.name: Cumin-Crusted Chicken with Avocado-Cucumber Salad

ingredients.name: Boneless, skinless chicken thighs
ingredients.prep: trimmed of excess fat and patted dry

ingredients.name: Olive oil
ingredients.prep: extra-virgin: 4 tbsp for the chicken (divided, plus more as needed), 1 tbsp in the salad

ingredients.name: Lime
ingredients.prep: 1 tbsp juice for the chicken (about ½ lime), 2 tbsp for the salad (about 1 lime), plus wedges for serving

ingredients.name: Kosher salt
ingredients.prep: 2 tsp on the chicken, 1 tsp in the salad

ingredients.name: Black pepper
ingredients.prep: freshly ground: 1 tsp on the chicken, ½ tsp in the salad

ingredients.name: Red onion
ingredients.prep: finely diced (¼ cup, about ¼ small onion)

instructions: In a large bowl, toss the chicken thighs with 2 tablespoons of the oil, 1 tablespoon lime juice, the salt, pepper, cumin, chili powder, paprika and cayenne. Let it marinate at room temperature for 10 minutes while you make the salad.

Salad: in a large bowl, toss the cucumbers, tomatoes, garlic, red onion, cilantro, 1 tablespoon olive oil, the salt, pepper, 2 tablespoons lime juice and the lemon juice. Add the avocado and gently toss once more. Cover and set aside.

Heat the remaining 2 tablespoons oil in a large skillet, preferably cast iron, over medium-high. Working in batches so the pan isn't crowded, cook the chicken in a single layer until golden brown on both sides and cooked through, 3 to 4 minutes per side. Move it to a serving platter to cool slightly, adding more oil to the pan if it gets dry.
Spoon the avocado-cucumber salad over the chicken and serve with lime wedges.
To grill instead: heat a grill to medium-high, lightly oil the grates, and cook the marinated thighs about 5 minutes per side, until nicely charred and 165°F inside.
From your cookbook, Everyday Eats, page 149 (Poultry).

recipes.name: Spiced Chicken and Chickpea Skillet

ingredients.name: Boneless, skinless chicken thighs
ingredients.prep: trimmed of excess fat and patted dry

ingredients.name: Kosher salt
ingredients.prep: 1 tsp on the chicken, ½ tsp with the vegetables

ingredients.name: Carrot
ingredients.prep: large, peeled and thinly sliced (about 1 cup)

ingredients.name: Lemon
ingredients.prep: zest of ½, plus 2 tbsp juice (about 1 lemon)

instructions: Put a rack in the middle of the oven and heat it to 375°F.
Season both sides of the chicken with 1 teaspoon of the salt, the paprika, coriander, cumin, turmeric and pepper, massaging the spices in.

Heat 1 tablespoon of the oil in a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high. Working in batches, brown the chicken in a single layer, about 3 minutes per side. It won't be cooked through yet. Move it to a clean plate.

Lower the heat to medium and add the remaining tablespoon of oil, the onion and the carrot with the remaining ½ teaspoon salt. Cook, stirring now and then, until tender, about 4 minutes. Add the garlic and cook 1 minute.

Stir in the tomato paste and harissa and cook until the tomato paste softens, about 2 minutes. Add the wine, lemon zest and lemon juice, scraping up the browned bits, and simmer until the wine has reduced by half, about 3 minutes.

Add the tomatoes, chickpeas and kale and bring to a simmer. Nestle the chicken and its juices back into the skillet. Carefully move it to the oven and cook uncovered 15 to 17 minutes, until the chicken is cooked through and the kale starts to crisp.
Let it cool slightly, then sprinkle with the oregano and feta (if using). Leftovers keep up to 3 days in the fridge. From your cookbook, Everyday Eats, page 150.

recipes.name: Kung Pao Ground Chicken

ingredients.name: Avocado oil
ingredients.prep: 2 tbsp for the chicken, 1 tbsp for the vegetables

ingredients.name: Green onions
ingredients.prep: 4, thinly sliced, white and green parts kept separate, plus more for garnish

ingredients.name: Crushed red pepper flakes
ingredients.prep: ½ to 1 tsp, depending on your heat preference

ingredients.name: Peanuts
ingredients.prep: dry roasted, roughly chopped, plus more for garnish (cashews for paleo)

ingredients.name: Lime
ingredients.prep: 1 tbsp freshly squeezed juice (about ½ lime)

ingredients.name: Cauliflower rice (optional)
ingredients.prep: prepared, or steamed rice, or lettuce leaves, for serving

instructions: Whisk the sesame oil, coconut aminos, broth, fish sauce, vinegar, coconut sugar and tapioca flour in a small bowl. Set aside.

Heat 2 tablespoons of the avocado oil in a large, deep skillet over medium-high. Add the chicken, salt and pepper and spread it into an even layer. Cook undisturbed until a golden crust forms on one side, about 3 minutes, then break it up and cook until no longer pink, about 4 more minutes. Move it to a clean plate and drain off any excess fat.

Add the remaining tablespoon of oil, the bell pepper, zucchini and white parts of the green onions. Cook, stirring now and then, until they begin to soften, about 2 minutes. Add the garlic, ginger and pepper flakes and cook until the garlic is golden and fragrant, about 2 more minutes.
Lower the heat to medium-low and return the chicken and its juices to the skillet. Whisk the sauce again and pour it in. Toss until the chicken is coated, about 2 minutes.
Turn the heat to low and stir in the peanuts, lime juice and green parts of the green onions. Serve over rice or in lettuce leaves, topped with more peanuts and green onions.
Leftovers keep up to 3 days in the fridge. From your cookbook, Everyday Eats, page 154.

recipes.name: Ground Turkey Enchilada Skillet

ingredients.name: Lime
ingredients.prep: 1 tbsp juice (about ½ lime), plus wedges for serving

ingredients.name: Cilantro
ingredients.prep: ¼ cup finely chopped leaves, plus more for garnish

ingredients.name: Corn tortillas
ingredients.prep: about 4, sliced into ¼-inch strips (1 cup)

instructions: Heat the oven to 400°F.

Heat the oil in a large oven-safe skillet or 3.5-quart braiser over medium-high. Cook the turkey and onion, breaking up the meat, until cooked through and no longer pink, about 7 minutes. Drain off the excess fat and return the turkey and onion to the pan.
Lower the heat to medium and add the cumin, garlic powder, chili powder, salt, pepper and green chiles. Cook, stirring, to toast the spices, about 2 minutes.

Pour in the enchilada sauce, beans, broth and lime juice and bring to a simmer. Add the cilantro and sliced tortillas, toss gently, then spread everything into a single layer and sprinkle the cheese over the top.
Bake uncovered until the cheese is golden brown, about 15 minutes. Let it rest 5 minutes so the sauce thickens a bit more.
Put a pile of shredded cabbage in the center of the skillet and scoop the mixture into four shallow bowls. Serve with sliced avocado, jalapeño (if using) and lime wedges.

Tortilla tip: if your tortillas are large, halve them before slicing into ¼-inch strips. Leftovers keep up to 3 days in the fridge, with the garnishes separate. Reheat in a 350°F oven 15 to 20 minutes or in the microwave. From your cookbook, Everyday Eats.

recipes.name: Hibachi-Inspired Steak Stir-Fry with Ginger Sauce

ingredients.name: Yellow onion
ingredients.prep: ½ medium (1 cup medium-diced) in the sauce, ½ medium (1 cup thinly sliced) in the stir-fry

ingredients.name: Coconut aminos
ingredients.prep: ¼ cup in the sauce, 2 tbsp in the stir-fry

ingredients.name: Kosher salt
ingredients.prep: ½ tsp in the sauce, 1 tsp on the steak, plus a pinch with the vegetables

ingredients.name: Black pepper
ingredients.prep: freshly ground: ½ tsp in the sauce, ½ tsp on the steak

ingredients.name: Filet or sirloin steak
ingredients.prep: patted dry and cut into 1-inch cubes

ingredients.name: Zucchini
ingredients.prep: small, cut in half crosswise, then each half quartered lengthwise

ingredients.name: Carrot
ingredients.prep: small, cut in half crosswise, then each half quartered lengthwise

instructions: Ginger sauce: blend the sauce ingredients in a food processor or blender until just smooth. Set aside. It keeps 3 days in the fridge.
Season the steak with the salt and pepper and toss to coat.

Heat the avocado oil in a large skillet over medium-high. Working in batches so the pan isn't crowded, sear the steak in a single layer until golden brown on all sides, about 2 minutes per side. Move it to a clean plate with a slotted spoon.
If the skillet is dry, add 1 tablespoon more avocado oil. Cook the onion, zucchini, carrots and a pinch of salt, tossing, until slightly tender, about 5 minutes.

Lower the heat to medium. Stir in the butter (if using), coconut aminos and sesame seeds, then return the steak and its juices to the pan. Cook, tossing, until the steak is coated and the sauce has reduced, about 2 minutes.
Serve over rice with the ginger sauce on the side for dipping. Keep the stir-fry and sauce in separate containers in the fridge up to 3 days. From your cookbook, Everyday Eats, page 174.

recipes.name: Calabrian Chile Meatball Orzo Skillet

ingredients.name: Calabrian peppers
ingredients.prep: jarred, chopped: 2 tbsp in the meatballs, 1 tbsp in the orzo

ingredients.name: Kosher salt
ingredients.prep: 1 tsp in the meatballs, 1 tsp in the orzo

ingredients.name: Shallot
ingredients.prep: large, halved and thinly sliced (½ cup)

ingredients.name: Fresh basil
ingredients.prep: ¼ cup torn leaves, for serving

instructions: Meatballs: in a large bowl, mix the beef, Calabrian peppers, egg, panko, salt, Italian seasoning, pepper, garlic and rosemary with clean hands until just combined. Don't overmix or they'll be tough. Form 16 meatballs, about 1 inch each.

Heat the oil in a large, deep skillet or 3.5-quart braiser with a lid over medium-high. Brown the meatballs in a single layer, 2 to 3 minutes per side. They don't need to be cooked through. Move them to a clean plate.
Orzo: lower the heat to medium, add the shallot and tomatoes and cook, stirring, until the tomatoes blister and burst, 3 to 4 minutes.
Stir in the salt, tomato paste and Calabrian peppers. Pour in the wine and cook, stirring, until reduced by half, about 2 minutes.

Add the orzo, broth and lemon zest and bring to a rapid simmer, then lower to a gentle simmer (about medium-low). Nestle the meatballs into the pan, cover, and cook about 10 minutes, stirring once halfway so the orzo doesn't stick, until the orzo is al dente and the meatballs are cooked through.
Off the heat, stir once more and sprinkle the mozzarella over the top. Cover for about 2 minutes to melt it. Top with the basil and divide among four shallow bowls.
Leftovers keep up to 3 days in the fridge. Reheat with a splash of broth. From your cookbook, Everyday Eats, page 173 (Beef, Pork, and Lamb).

recipes.name: Honey-Orange Pork and Snap Pea Stir-Fry

ingredients.name: Orange
ingredients.prep: 1 tbsp grated zest, plus 1 tbsp freshly squeezed juice

ingredients.name: Pork tenderloin
ingredients.prep: silver skin removed, patted dry, and cut into 1-inch cubes

ingredients.name: Shallot
ingredients.prep: large, halved and thinly sliced (½ cup)

instructions: Sauce: whisk all the sauce ingredients in a small bowl until combined. Set aside.
In a large bowl, toss the pork with the salt, pepper and tapioca flour until coated.

Heat the avocado oil in a large, deep nonstick skillet over medium-high. Add the pork in a single layer and cook undisturbed until a golden-brown crust forms on one side, 3 to 4 minutes. Flip and keep cooking, tossing now and then, until browned on both sides and cooked through, 3 to 4 more minutes. Move the pork to a clean plate with a slotted spoon.

Lower the heat to medium. Cook the shallot for 1 minute until it begins to soften. Add the snap peas and 2 tablespoons water, scraping up the browned bits, and cook, stirring now and then, until the water has evaporated and the peas are bright green and slightly tender but still crunchy, about 4 minutes.
Return the pork and its juices to the pan and toss. Pour in the sauce, stir, and bring to a simmer. Cook, tossing, until the pork and peas are well coated, about 2 more minutes.
Sprinkle with toasted sesame seeds and serve over rice. Leftovers keep up to 3 days in the fridge. From your cookbook, Everyday Eats.

recipes.name: Creamy Peperoncini Chicken

ingredients.name: Boneless, skinless chicken breasts
ingredients.prep: small, pounded to an even ½ inch

ingredients.name: Peperoncini
ingredients.prep: jarred: ½ cup sliced peppers, drained, plus 3 tbsp of the brine

ingredients.name: Lemon
ingredients.prep: 1 tbsp freshly squeezed juice (about ½ lemon)

instructions: Cover the chicken breasts with parchment or plastic wrap and pound to an even ½-inch thickness. Season both sides with the salt, pepper and Italian seasoning, then sprinkle with the flour so the pieces are evenly coated.

Heat the oil in a large, deep skillet or 3.5-quart braiser over medium-high. Cook the chicken until golden brown on both sides, 2 to 3 minutes per side. It won't be cooked through yet. Move it to a clean plate.
Lower the heat to medium, add the butter and let it melt. Cook the onion and bell pepper, stirring, until they begin to soften, about 3 minutes.
Add the garlic and peperoncini brine, scraping up the browned bits, and cook until the liquid has reduced by half, 1 to 2 minutes.

Add both mustards, the broth, lemon juice and peperoncini peppers, stir, and bring to a rapid simmer. Lower to a gentle simmer (about medium-low) and stir in the yogurt and Parmesan until the sauce is smooth. Don't let it boil or the yogurt will curdle.
Nestle the chicken and its juices into the pan and cook, uncovered and gently simmering, until the sauce thickens and the chicken is cooked through, about 5 more minutes. Finish with the parsley.
Leftovers keep up to 3 days in the fridge. Reheat gently over medium-low with a splash of broth. From your cookbook, Everyday Eats, page 146.

recipes.name: Slow Cooker or Pressure Cooker BBQ Beef Lettuce Wraps

ingredients.name: Red onion
ingredients.prep: small: 1 cup halved and thinly sliced for the beef, 1 more cup for serving

ingredients.name: Pickled jalapeños
ingredients.prep: 2 tbsp of the brine for the beef, plus slices for serving

ingredients.name: Barbecue sauce
ingredients.prep: no-sugar-added: ½ cup in the sauce, ¼ cup stirred in at the end, plus more for serving

ingredients.name: Flap, flank or skirt steak
ingredients.prep: flank steak, trimmed of excess fat, patted dry, and cut into 4 equal-size pieces

instructions: Slow cooker: whisk the garlic, red onion, tomato paste, jalapeño brine, ½ cup of the barbecue sauce, broth, coconut sugar, mustard, paprika and garlic powder in the slow cooker. Season the steak with the salt and pepper and nestle it into the sauce. Cover and cook on high 4 hours or on low 8 hours, until fall-apart tender.

Pressure cooker instead: whisk the same sauce in the pressure cooker, nestle in the seasoned steak, seal the lid and vent, and cook on manual or pressure-cook for 60 minutes. Release the pressure manually by turning the valve and letting it vent completely.
