Move the steak to a rimmed sheet pan and shred it with two forks. Add the remaining ¼ cup barbecue sauce, the lime juice and about ½ cup of the cooking liquid and toss.
To serve, layer two lettuce leaves on each plate, add the beef and finish with red onion, avocado, pickles, pickled jalapeños, more barbecue sauce and cilantro.

Leftovers keep up to 4 days in the fridge, with the lettuce and toppings separate. Reheat the beef in a skillet over medium heat or in the microwave in 1-minute bursts. From your cookbook, Everyday Eats, page 169 (Beef, Pork, and Lamb).

recipes.name: Creamy Sun-Dried Tomato Basil Chicken

ingredients.name: Boneless, skinless chicken breasts
ingredients.prep: small, trimmed of excess fat and patted dry

ingredients.name: Kosher salt
ingredients.prep: 1 tsp on the chicken, ½ tsp in the sauce

ingredients.name: Black pepper
ingredients.prep: freshly ground: ½ tsp on the chicken, ½ tsp in the sauce

ingredients.name: Shallot
ingredients.prep: large, halved and thinly sliced (½ cup)

ingredients.name: Fresh basil
ingredients.prep: ½ cup thinly sliced leaves, plus more for garnish

instructions: Season both sides of the chicken with 1 teaspoon of the salt and ½ teaspoon of the pepper. Dredge each piece in the flour in a large, shallow bowl until coated on both sides, shaking off the excess.

Heat the oil in a large, deep skillet or 3.5-quart braiser over medium-high. Cook the chicken until golden brown on both sides, 2 to 3 minutes per side. It will finish cooking in the sauce. Move it to a clean plate.

Lower the heat to medium and add the cherry tomatoes, pepper flakes, garlic, shallot and sun-dried tomatoes. Cook, stirring, until the cherry tomatoes blister and soften, about 4 minutes. It's fine if they burst.
Stir in the tomato paste and broth and cook, stirring, until the liquid has reduced by half, about 3 minutes.

Add the coconut milk, the remaining ½ teaspoon salt and ½ teaspoon pepper and bring to a rapid simmer, then lower to a gentle simmer (about medium-low). Nestle the chicken into the sauce and top with the basil. Simmer uncovered until the sauce thickens and the chicken is cooked through, 7 to 10 minutes.

Take it off the heat and stir in the lemon juice. Garnish with more basil and toasted pine nuts, if you like. Leftovers keep up to 3 days in the fridge. From your cookbook, Everyday Eats, page 153 (Poultry).

recipes.name: Skillet Creamed Corn Chicken

ingredients.name: Boneless, skinless chicken breasts
ingredients.prep: trimmed of excess fat, patted dry, and pounded to ½ inch

ingredients.name: Kosher salt
ingredients.prep: 1 tsp on the chicken, 1 tsp with the corn

ingredients.name: Black pepper
ingredients.prep: freshly ground: ½ tsp on the chicken, ½ tsp with the corn

ingredients.name: Poblano pepper
ingredients.prep: large, seeded and sliced into ¼-inch strips

ingredients.name: Red onion
ingredients.prep: small, halved and thinly sliced (½ cup)

ingredients.name: Lime
ingredients.prep: zest of ½, plus 2 tbsp juice (about 1 lime), and wedges for serving

instructions: Heat the oven to 375°F. Cover the chicken breasts with parchment or plastic wrap and pound to an even ½-inch thickness.

Season both sides with 1 teaspoon of the salt, ½ teaspoon of the pepper and the chili powder. Dredge each piece in the flour in a large, shallow bowl until coated on both sides, shaking off the excess.

Heat the oil in a large oven-safe skillet or 3.5-quart braiser over medium-high. Cook the chicken until golden brown on both sides, 2 to 3 minutes per side. It will finish cooking in the oven. Move it to a clean plate.
Lower the heat to medium. Cook the poblano, onion and garlic, stirring, until they begin to soften, about 3 minutes.
Add the corn kernels, the remaining 1 teaspoon salt and the remaining ½ teaspoon pepper and cook, stirring, until the corn begins to soften, about 2 more minutes.
Lower the heat to medium-low and stir in the cream cheese, broth, lime zest and lime juice until well combined.

Nestle the chicken back into the skillet and sprinkle the Monterey Jack over it. Bake uncovered until the cheese is melted and the chicken is cooked through, 12 to 15 minutes. Garnish with the cilantro and serve with lime wedges.
Leftovers keep up to 3 days in the fridge. Reheat in a skillet over medium heat with a splash of broth. From your cookbook, Everyday Eats.

recipes.name: Tangy Thai Braised Chicken

ingredients.name: Bone-in, skin-on chicken leg quarters
ingredients.prep: small, whole (or 8 thighs), trimmed of excess fat and patted dry

ingredients.name: Shallot
ingredients.prep: large (1 cup halved and thinly sliced)

ingredients.name: Fresh ginger (1-inch piece)
ingredients.prep: 1-inch piece, peeled and cut into thin matchsticks

ingredients.name: Cauliflower rice (optional)
ingredients.prep: prepared, or steamed rice, for serving

instructions: Heat the oven to 375°F.
Braising liquid: whisk the coconut aminos, coconut milk, broth, curry paste, fish sauce, coconut sugar and garlic in a medium bowl until very well combined. Set aside.

Season both sides of the chicken with the salt and pepper. Heat the oil in a large, deep oven-safe skillet or 3.5-quart braiser over medium-high. Arrange the chicken skin side down in a single layer and cook until a deep golden-brown crust forms, 6 to 7 minutes. It won't be cooked through yet.
Take the pan off the heat and flip the chicken skin side up. Scatter the shallots, ginger and green onions over and around it, then pour the braising liquid around and over the chicken.
Bake uncovered until the chicken is cooked through and fork-tender, about 50 minutes. Let it rest about 5 minutes, then garnish with the Thai basil and cilantro.
Serve over rice in four shallow bowls, ladling the broth over and around the chicken, with lime wedges. Leftovers keep up to 3 days in the fridge. From your cookbook, Everyday Eats.

recipes.name: Chipotle Chimichurri Steak Bite Bowls

ingredients.name: Chipotle chiles in adobo
ingredients.prep: 2 canned peppers in adobo sauce, minced (about 2 tbsp)

ingredients.name: Cilantro
ingredients.prep: 1 cup roughly chopped leaves and tender stems for the chimichurri, plus more for serving

ingredients.name: Fresh parsley
ingredients.prep: 1 cup roughly chopped leaves and tender stems

ingredients.name: Kosher salt
ingredients.prep: ½ tsp in the chimichurri, 2 tsp on the steak

ingredients.name: Flap, flank or skirt steak
ingredients.prep: sirloin or flank, trimmed of excess fat, patted dry, and cut into 1-inch cubes

ingredients.name: Cauliflower rice (optional)
ingredients.prep: prepared, or steamed rice, for serving

instructions: Chimichurri: pulse the chipotles, cilantro, parsley, garlic, olive oil, lime juice, vinegar and ½ teaspoon salt in a food processor or blender until combined but still slightly chunky, with flecks of herbs visible. Set aside. For the best flavor, let it come to room temperature and stir well before serving.
Cut the steak into 1-inch cubes and season generously with 2 teaspoons salt, the pepper and the cumin. Toss until coated.

Heat the avocado oil in a large skillet, preferably cast iron, over medium-high. Working in batches so the pan isn't crowded, sear the steak cubes in a single layer, undisturbed, for 2 minutes, until a deep golden crust forms on one side. Flip and cook 1 to 2 minutes more. You want a quick sear, not overcooked steak. Move it to a clean plate and let it rest a couple of minutes.
Bowls: divide rice among four bowls. Add plenty of romaine, a big scoop of steak bites and the pico de gallo. Finish with a generous dollop of chimichurri and top with cilantro.

Leftovers keep up to 3 days in the fridge, with the chimichurri separate. Reheat the steak in a skillet over medium-low or in the microwave just until warmed. From your cookbook, Everyday Eats, page 166.

recipes.name: Sloppy Janes

ingredients.name: Avocado oil
ingredients.prep: 2 tbsp on the potatoes, 2 tbsp for the beef mixture

ingredients.name: Kosher salt
ingredients.prep: ½ tsp on the potatoes, 1 tsp in the beef mixture

ingredients.name: Fresh parsley
ingredients.prep: finely chopped leaves, optional for garnish

instructions: Heat the oven to 400°F and line a sheet pan with parchment paper.

Scrub and pat dry the sweet potatoes and set them on the pan. Pierce each about six times with a fork, drizzle with 2 tablespoons oil, rub it in, and sprinkle with ½ teaspoon salt. Bake until tender, about 40 minutes.
Meanwhile, heat the remaining 2 tablespoons oil in a large skillet over medium. Cook the onion, bell pepper and garlic, stirring, until tender, about 4 minutes.
Add the beef and cook, breaking it up, until cooked through and no longer pink, about 7 minutes. Drain off the excess fat and return the beef to the pan.

Stir in the salt, pepper, chili powder, tomato paste, mustard and coconut aminos until the meat is coated, 3 to 4 more minutes. Turn the heat to low, cover, and keep warm until the potatoes are ready.
Let the potatoes cool enough to handle. Carve a slit in the top of each, fluff the inside with a fork, and spoon the beef mixture into the center. Garnish with parsley if you like.
Leftovers keep up to 3 days in the fridge. Reheat in the microwave in 1-minute bursts, stirring the filling after each. From your cookbook, Everyday Eats.

recipes.name: Chorizo and Sweet Potato Street Tacos

ingredients.name: Avocado oil
ingredients.prep: only if the skillet seems dry

ingredients.name: White onion
ingredients.prep: ½ medium (1 cup finely diced) for the filling, plus ¼ small (¼ cup finely diced) for serving

ingredients.name: Kosher salt
ingredients.prep: plus a little to taste in the salsa

ingredients.name: Avocado
ingredients.prep: large: ½ in the salsa, ½ cubed for the tacos

ingredients.name: Lime
ingredients.prep: 1 tbsp juice (about ½ lime), plus wedges for serving

ingredients.name: Flour tortillas (4-inch)
ingredients.prep: or corn tortillas for gluten-free, or grain-free tortillas

instructions: Line a plate with paper towels. Cook the chorizo in a large skillet over medium-high, breaking it up, until browned, crumbly and fully cooked with no pink left, 7 to 9 minutes. Move it to the plate with a slotted spoon.
Lower the heat to medium, adding the oil only if the skillet seems dry. Cook the onion, poblano, sweet potato and salt, stirring often, until the sweet potato is tender, about 8 minutes.
Return the chorizo to the skillet and toss until it's warmed through and combined, 2 to 3 minutes. Turn the heat to low to keep warm.

Avocado salsa: blend the ½ avocado, salsa verde and lime juice until smooth in a small blender or with an immersion blender in a wide-mouth jar. Add salt to taste. It keeps up to 3 days in the fridge.
Warm the tortillas one at a time in a dry skillet over medium heat, about 30 seconds per side, or char them over a gas flame for a few seconds.

Fill the tortillas with the chorizo and sweet potato mixture, top with a dollop of avocado salsa and the cubed avocado, and finish with the queso fresco (if using), onion and cilantro. Serve with lime wedges.
Leftovers keep up to 3 days in the fridge, with the tortillas, salsa and toppings separate. Reheat the filling in a skillet over medium. From your cookbook, Everyday Eats.

recipes.name: Italian Sausage with Brothy White Beans and Kale

ingredients.name: Shallot
ingredients.prep: large, halved and thinly sliced (1 cup)

ingredients.name: Lemon
ingredients.prep: zest of ½, plus 1 tbsp juice (about ½ lemon)

ingredients.name: Fresh thyme
ingredients.prep: 1 tsp leaves (or ½ tsp dried), plus more for garnish

ingredients.name: Parmesan
ingredients.prep: freshly grated, for serving (omit for dairy-free); the book gives no amount, so ¼ cup is my estimate

instructions: Heat the oil in a large skillet or 3.5-quart braiser with a lid over medium. Sear the sausage links until browned on both sides, 3 to 4 minutes per side. They don't need to be cooked through yet. Move them to a plate.
In the same skillet, cook the shallots, garlic, pepper flakes (if using), salt, pepper and Italian seasoning, stirring, until softened, about 2 minutes.
Pour in the wine, scraping up the browned bits, and simmer 2 minutes to reduce slightly.

Stir in the tomato paste. Add the beans, broth, lemon zest and thyme, bring to a rapid simmer, then lower to a gentle simmer (about medium-low). Nestle the sausages back in, cover, and cook 10 minutes so the flavors meld and the sausage finishes cooking.
Stir in the kale and lemon juice and let the kale wilt into the broth, 2 to 3 minutes. Take it off the heat.
Divide the brothy beans among four shallow bowls and top each with a sausage. Garnish with Parmesan (if using) and fresh thyme.
Leftovers keep up to 3 days in the fridge. Reheat in a skillet over medium. From your cookbook, Everyday Eats.

recipes.name: Smashed Lamb Burger Tacos with Harissa-Yogurt Sauce

ingredients.name: Kosher salt
ingredients.prep: ¼ tsp in the sauce, 1½ tsp in the burgers

ingredients.name: Black pepper
ingredients.prep: freshly ground: ¼ tsp in the sauce, ½ tsp in the burgers

ingredients.name: Avocado oil
ingredients.prep: 1 tbsp to start, more for each batch; the book gives no total, so 2 tbsp is my estimate

ingredients.name: Flour tortillas (6-inch)
ingredients.prep: or almond-flour tortillas for gluten-free and grain-free

ingredients.name: Red onion
ingredients.prep: small (1 cup halved and thinly sliced)

instructions: Sauce: whisk the yogurt, harissa, lemon juice, salt and pepper in a small bowl and keep it in the fridge until serving. It keeps 5 days.

Burgers: in a medium bowl, mix the lamb, garlic, cumin, coriander, oregano, allspice, salt and pepper with clean hands until just combined, without overworking the meat. Roll into 8 equal balls, about 2 inches each.

Heat 1 tablespoon of the oil in a large skillet or griddle over medium-high. Place 1 or 2 lamb balls in the pan, set a tortilla on top of each, and press down hard with a grilling press or sturdy spatula to smash each into a thin patty. Cook undisturbed 3 to 4 minutes, until the meat is browned and cooked through.

Scrape under each burger with a stiff spatula and flip so the tortilla is on the bottom. Cook 1 to 2 more minutes, until the tortilla is warm and slightly crisp. Move to a platter and repeat with the rest, adding oil for each batch. Don't stack the tacos or the tortillas get soggy.
For each taco, add a handful of romaine, tomatoes, onion, dill and feta, and drizzle generously with the harissa-yogurt sauce. Serve immediately.
From your cookbook, Everyday Eats, page 183 (Beef, Pork, and Lamb).

recipes.name: Red Curry Pork Stir-Fry

ingredients.name: Kosher salt
ingredients.prep: 1 tsp with the pork, ½ tsp with the beans

ingredients.name: Yardlong beans
ingredients.prep: trimmed into 2-inch pieces (French or green beans work too)

ingredients.name: Lime
ingredients.prep: 1 tbsp freshly squeezed juice (about ½ lime)

ingredients.name: Cilantro
ingredients.prep: ¼ cup roughly chopped leaves and tender stems

instructions: Heat the avocado oil in a large, deep skillet or wok over medium-high. Add the pork and press it down into a single layer with the back of a spatula. Cook undisturbed until one side is crisp and golden, about 4 minutes. Add 1 teaspoon of the salt and keep cooking, breaking up the pork, until cooked through and no longer pink, about 3 more minutes. Move it to a clean plate with a slotted spoon.
Lower the heat to medium and add the sesame oil and shallots. Cook, stirring, until softened, about 2 minutes.
Add the curry paste, yardlong beans, the remaining ½ teaspoon salt and the pepper. Cook, tossing often, until the beans are crisp-tender, about 5 minutes.
Add the garlic, coconut aminos, fish sauce and coconut sugar. Stir, bring to a simmer, and cook, tossing, until the beans are well coated, 2 to 3 more minutes.
Lower the heat to medium-low and return the pork and its juices to the pan. Stir in the lime juice, basil and cilantro until the herbs just wilt. Serve right away over rice.

Leftovers keep up to 3 days in the fridge. Reheat in a skillet or wok over medium heat so the pork stays tender and the beans crisp. From your cookbook, Everyday Eats, page 191 (Beef, Pork, and Lamb).

recipes.name: Chili Crisp Citrus Salmon

ingredients.name: Shallot
ingredients.prep: large (½ cup halved and thinly sliced)

ingredients.name: Kosher salt
ingredients.prep: ½ tsp in the pan, ½ tsp on the salmon

ingredients.name: Black pepper
ingredients.prep: freshly ground: ¼ tsp in the pan, ¼ tsp on the salmon

ingredients.name: Navel oranges
ingredients.prep: medium, peeled and cut into ¼-inch rounds (see the book's note)

ingredients.name: Salmon fillets
ingredients.prep: 6-ounce skinless center-cut, patted dry, pin bones removed

instructions: Put a rack in the center of the oven and heat it to 400°F.

Heat the avocado oil and sesame oil in a large, deep oven-safe skillet or 3.5-quart braiser over medium-high. Cook the shallot, green onions, ½ teaspoon of the salt and ¼ teaspoon of the pepper, stirring, until just tender, about 2 minutes.

Add the orange rounds, coconut aminos, honey, vinegar and chili crisp, stir, and bring to a simmer. Nestle the salmon into the skillet and spoon some of the sauce over it. Sprinkle the tops with the remaining ½ teaspoon salt and ¼ teaspoon pepper.
Bake until the salmon is cooked through and flakes easily with a fork, 8 to 10 minutes.

Garnish with mint and serve over rice with a drizzle of extra chili crisp. To peel the oranges, slice off the top and bottom, then use a paring knife to cut away the rind and white pith in curving slices, then cut into rounds.
From your cookbook, Everyday Eats, page 222.

recipes.name: Harissa Salmon Bites with Sesame Cucumber Salad

ingredients.name: Lemon
ingredients.prep: 2 tbsp juice in the salad (about 1 lemon) and 2 tbsp in the glaze (about 1 lemon)

ingredients.name: Kosher salt
ingredients.prep: ½ tsp in the salad, 1½ tsp on the salmon

ingredients.name: Black pepper
ingredients.prep: freshly ground: ½ tsp in the salad, ½ tsp on the salmon

ingredients.name: Red onion
ingredients.prep: small (1 cup halved and thinly sliced)

ingredients.name: Cilantro
ingredients.prep: ½ cup roughly chopped leaves, plus more for garnish

ingredients.name: Salmon
ingredients.prep: skinless center-cut, patted dry, pin bones removed, cut into 1-inch cubes

ingredients.name: Cauliflower rice (optional)
ingredients.prep: prepared, or steamed rice, or gluten-free orzo

instructions: Put racks in the center and at the top of the oven and heat it to 425°F. Line a sheet pan with parchment paper.
Salad: whisk the yogurt, tahini, sesame oil, 2 tablespoons lemon juice, garlic, ½ teaspoon salt and ½ teaspoon pepper in a large bowl. It will look very thick but thins out once the vegetables go in.

Cut the cucumbers in half lengthwise, scoop out the seeds, and slice into half-moons (about 4 cups). Add them to the dressing with the onion and toss until the cucumbers release some liquid and the dressing thins. Add the cilantro, dill and sesame seeds, toss again, and chill until the salmon is ready.

Salmon: toss the salmon cubes with the arrowroot, paprika, garlic powder, oregano, 1½ teaspoons salt, ½ teaspoon pepper and the avocado oil until evenly coated. Spread on the pan in a single layer with space between pieces and bake on the middle rack for 10 minutes.
Meanwhile, whisk the harissa, the other 2 tablespoons lemon juice and the honey in a small bowl.

After 10 minutes, take the pan out and pour the harissa mixture over the salmon, tossing to coat. Turn the broiler on high and broil on the top rack until the salmon is slightly charred, about 3 more minutes, watching closely so it doesn't burn. Let it cool slightly.
Divide the rice or orzo among four shallow bowls, top with the sesame cucumber salad and the salmon, and garnish with more cilantro and sesame seeds. From your cookbook, Everyday Eats, page 214.

recipes.name: Sheet Pan Shrimp Fajita Tacos

ingredients.name: Mini bell peppers
ingredients.prep: seeded and sliced into thin rounds

ingredients.name: Red onion
ingredients.prep: small (1 cup halved and thinly sliced)

ingredients.name: Avocado oil
ingredients.prep: 2 tbsp on the vegetables, 2 tbsp on the shrimp

ingredients.name: Kosher salt
ingredients.prep: ½ tsp on the vegetables, 1½ tsp on the shrimp

ingredients.name: Shrimp
ingredients.prep: peeled, deveined, tail-off (36/40 count), patted dry

ingredients.name: Lime
ingredients.prep: zest of ½, plus wedges for serving

instructions: Heat the oven to 425°F and line a sheet pan with parchment paper.

Put the bell peppers, onion and serrano (if using) on the pan. Drizzle with 2 tablespoons of the oil, ½ teaspoon of the salt and ½ teaspoon of the pepper, toss, and spread into an even layer. Roast until just softened, about 10 minutes.

Meanwhile, toss the shrimp in a large bowl with the remaining 2 tablespoons oil, 1½ teaspoons salt, ½ teaspoon pepper, the chili powder, garlic powder, paprika, cumin, oregano and lime zest until evenly coated.
Take the vegetables out, add the shrimp, toss, and spread into an even layer. Roast until the shrimp are cooked through, about 10 minutes.
If using tortillas, warm them one at a time in a dry skillet over medium heat, about 30 seconds per side, or char them over a gas flame for a few seconds.

For each taco, spread mashed avocado on the bottom of a tortilla (or inside a lettuce cup), fill with the shrimp and vegetables, and finish with cilantro and a drizzle of salsa. Serve with lime wedges.

Leftovers keep up to 2 days in the fridge, with the tortillas and toppings separate. Reheat quickly in a skillet over medium or in the air fryer at 350°F for 3 to 4 minutes, and avoid the microwave, which makes shrimp rubbery. From your cookbook, Everyday Eats.

recipes.name: Garlic Shrimp Stir-Fry

ingredients.name: Red onion
ingredients.prep: small (1 cup halved and thinly sliced)

ingredients.name: Shrimp
ingredients.prep: peeled, deveined, tail-off (31/35 count), patted dry

instructions: Sauce: whisk the coconut aminos, fish sauce, broth, sesame oil, honey, garlic, ginger and tapioca flour in a small bowl until well combined. Set aside.
Heat the oil in a large, deep nonstick skillet over medium. Cook the broccoli, bell pepper and onion, stirring, until slightly tender, 4 to 5 minutes.
Add the shrimp, salt and pepper and cook, tossing, until the shrimp begin to turn pink. They don't need to be cooked through, since they finish in the sauce.
Pour in the sauce and cook, tossing often, until the shrimp are cooked through and the sauce has thickened, about 4 more minutes. Toss once more to coat.
Serve over rice with a drizzle of chili crisp, if you like.

Leftovers keep up to 3 days in the fridge. Reheat in a hot skillet or wok just until warmed through, about 2 minutes, and avoid the microwave, which makes shrimp rubbery. From your cookbook, Everyday Eats, page 204.

recipes.name: Skillet Unstuffed Cabbage Rolls

ingredients.name: Black pepper
ingredients.prep: freshly ground, plus more to taste

ingredients.name: Basmati rice
ingredients.prep: rinsed until the water runs clear

ingredients.name: Lemon
ingredients.prep: 1 tbsp juice (about ½ lemon), plus wedges for serving

ingredients.name: Fresh parsley
ingredients.prep: ¼ cup finely chopped, plus more for serving

ingredients.name: Fresh dill
ingredients.prep: ¼ cup finely chopped, plus more for serving

ingredients.name: Plain Greek yogurt
ingredients.prep: whole-milk, optional for topping (omit for dairy-free); the book gives no amount, so 1 cup is my estimate

instructions: Heat the oil in a large, deep skillet or 3.5-quart braiser with a lid over medium-high. Cook the onion and beef, breaking up the meat, until browned and no longer pink and the onions are tender, about 7 minutes. Drain off the excess fat and return the beef and onions to the pan.
Lower the heat to medium and add the salt, pepper, allspice, cumin and paprika. Cook, tossing, until the spices are fragrant, about 2 minutes.
Add the cabbage and garlic and cook, tossing, until the cabbage is slightly softened, about 3 minutes. Stir in the tomato paste and tamari until well combined.

Add the rice, tomatoes, broth, coconut sugar, lemon juice, parsley and dill and stir. Bring to a rapid simmer, then lower to a gentle simmer (about medium-low), cover, and cook 20 minutes. Take the skillet off the heat and keep it covered 10 more minutes so the rice steams until tender.
Fluff the rice with a fork and garnish with more dill and parsley. Scoop into bowls and top with a dollop of yogurt, if you like, with lemon wedges on the side.

Leftovers keep up to 3 days in the fridge, separate from the toppings. Reheat gently in a skillet over medium or in the microwave in 1-minute bursts, stirring after each. From your cookbook, Everyday Eats.

recipes.name: Sheet Pan Kofta Meatballs with Veggies

ingredients.name: Red bell pepper
ingredients.prep: medium, seeded and sliced into ¼-inch strips

ingredients.name: Yellow bell pepper
ingredients.prep: medium, seeded and sliced into ¼-inch strips

ingredients.name: Kosher salt
ingredients.prep: ½ tsp on the vegetables, 1 tsp in the meatballs

ingredients.name: Black pepper
ingredients.prep: freshly ground: ¼ tsp on the vegetables, ½ tsp in the meatballs

ingredients.name: Ground cumin
ingredients.prep: ½ tsp on the vegetables, 2 tsp in the meatballs

ingredients.name: Cilantro
ingredients.prep: 2 tbsp finely chopped leaves in the meatballs, plus leaves for serving

instructions: Put a rack at the top of the oven and heat it to 425°F.
Put the bell peppers and onion on a large sheet pan, drizzle with the oil, and season with ½ teaspoon salt, ¼ teaspoon pepper and ½ teaspoon cumin. Toss and spread into a single layer.

In a medium bowl, mix the lamb, egg, panko, garlic, 2 teaspoons cumin, the coriander, allspice, cayenne (if using), 1 teaspoon salt, ½ teaspoon pepper and 2 tablespoons cilantro with clean hands until well combined. Roll into 1½-inch meatballs and nestle them onto the pan with the vegetables.
Bake on the top rack until the meatballs are golden on top and no longer pink in the center and the vegetables are tender, about 15 minutes.
To serve, put 1 to 2 tablespoons hummus in a shallow bowl or on a small plate, set the meatballs and vegetables on it, and garnish with cilantro. Serve with warm pita, if using.

Leftovers keep up to 3 days in the fridge. Reheat on a sheet pan in a 350°F oven for 10 to 12 minutes, in a skillet over medium, or in the microwave in 1-minute bursts. From your cookbook, Everyday Eats.

recipes.name: Sweet and Savory Korean-Style Beef Bowls

ingredients.name: Lime
ingredients.prep: 1 tbsp freshly squeezed juice (about ½ lime)

ingredients.name: Green onions
ingredients.prep: 3, thinly sliced on the diagonal, white and green parts kept separate

instructions: Sauce: whisk the sesame oil, coconut aminos, fish sauce, ginger, coconut sugar, gochujang, lime juice and garlic in a small bowl. Set aside.
Heat the avocado oil in a large, deep skillet over medium-high. Cook the white onion, stirring often, until softened, about 2 minutes.

Add the beef and press it down into a single layer with the back of a spatula. Cook undisturbed until one side is crisp and golden brown, about 4 minutes. Break it up and keep cooking until cooked through and no longer pink, about 3 more minutes. Drain off the excess fat and return the beef to the pan.
Add the salt, pepper, white parts of the green onions and the sauce. Cook, stirring, until the sauce coats the meat and reduces slightly, 3 to 4 more minutes.
Put prepared rice in each bowl, spoon the beef and sauce over it, and garnish with the sesame seeds and the green parts of the green onions. Serve with plenty of kimchi on the side.
Leftovers keep up to 3 days in the fridge, with the rice and kimchi separate. Reheat the beef in a skillet over medium or in the microwave in 1-minute bursts. From your cookbook, Everyday Eats.

recipes.name: Crunchy Coconut Shrimp Bowls with Spicy Aioli

ingredients.name: Sriracha
ingredients.prep: 1 to 2 tbsp, depending on your heat preference

ingredients.name: Lime
ingredients.prep: 1 tbsp juice (about ½ lime) in the aioli, plus wedges for serving

ingredients.name: Kosher salt
ingredients.prep: ¼ tsp in the aioli, ½ tsp in the slaw, 1½ tsp on the shrimp

ingredients.name: Shrimp
ingredients.prep: peeled, deveined, tail-off (36/40 count), patted dry

ingredients.name: Black sesame seeds
ingredients.prep: optional, for garnish; the book gives no amount

instructions: Aioli: whisk the mayo, sriracha, lime juice and ¼ teaspoon salt in a small bowl until well combined. Set aside.
Slaw: toss the cabbage, green onions, sesame oil, vinegar and ½ teaspoon salt in a medium bowl. Set aside.

Line a plate with paper towels. Heat the avocado oil in a large skillet over medium-high. Add the shrimp and sprinkle with 1 teaspoon of the salt and the pepper. Cook until golden brown on each side and cooked through, 2 to 3 minutes per side. Move them to the plate with a slotted spoon.
Lower the heat to medium. Add the panko, coconut and the remaining ½ teaspoon salt and toast, tossing, until golden brown, 2 to 3 minutes, watching so it doesn't burn. Set aside.

Divide the rice among four bowls and top with the sesame slaw and shrimp. Sprinkle the coconut-panko over the top, put the sliced avocado to the side, and drizzle generously with the spicy aioli, then cilantro. Add sesame seeds if you like and serve with lime wedges.
From your cookbook, Everyday Eats, page 211 (Fresh Catch).

recipes.name: Thai-Inspired Shredded Beef Bowls (Slow or Pressure Cooker)

ingredients.name: Garlic
ingredients.prep: minced: 4 for the beef, 2 for the salad

ingredients.name: Fish sauce
ingredients.prep: 1 tbsp for the beef, 4 tsp for the salad

ingredients.name: Thai chiles
ingredients.prep: 1 to 3 minced for the beef and 1 to 3 for the salad (see the Tipsy Noodles note for heat)

ingredients.name: Flap, flank or skirt steak
ingredients.prep: flap or flank, trimmed of excess fat, patted dry, cut into 4 equal-size pieces

ingredients.name: Kosher salt
ingredients.prep: plus a pinch for the salad

ingredients.name: Lime
ingredients.prep: zest of ½ and 2 tbsp juice (about 1 lime), plus wedges for serving

ingredients.name: Mini bell peppers
ingredients.prep: seeded and sliced into thin strips

ingredients.name: Red onion
ingredients.prep: small (½ cup halved and thinly sliced)

instructions: Slow cooker: whisk the garlic, ginger, coconut sugar, coconut aminos, fish sauce, peanut butter and Thai chiles in the slow cooker. Season the steak with the salt and pepper and nestle it in. Cook on high 4 hours or on low 8 hours, until fall-apart tender.

Pressure cooker instead: whisk the same sauce plus the ½ cup broth in the pressure cooker, nestle in the seasoned steak, seal the lid and vent, and cook on manual or pressure-cook for 60 minutes. Release the pressure manually by turning the valve and letting it vent completely.
Move the steak pieces to a rimmed sheet pan and shred with two forks. Return the meat and its juices to the cooker, add the lime zest and lime juice, and toss. Keep warm while you make the salad.

Veggie salad: toss the mini bell peppers, onion, carrots, Thai chiles, garlic, rice vinegar, 4 teaspoons fish sauce and a pinch of salt in a large bowl. Set aside at least 10 minutes to lightly pickle.
Divide the beef among bowls with the rice and veggie salad, top with cilantro and basil, and serve with lime wedges.

Leftovers keep up to 4 days in the fridge, with the salad separate. Reheat the beef in a skillet over medium or in the microwave in 1-minute bursts. From your cookbook, Everyday Eats, page 192 (Beef, Pork, and Lamb).

recipes.name: Sheet Pan Chipotle-Honey Butter Salmon

ingredients.name: Sweet potato
ingredients.prep: large, unpeeled and cut into ½-inch dice (about 2 cups)

ingredients.name: Kosher salt
ingredients.prep: 1 tsp on the vegetables, 1 tsp on the salmon

ingredients.name: Lime
ingredients.prep: zest of ½ and 2 tbsp juice (about 1 lime), plus wedges for serving

ingredients.name: Cilantro
ingredients.prep: 1 tbsp finely chopped leaves, plus more for garnish

ingredients.name: Salmon fillets
ingredients.prep: 6-ounce skinless center-cut, patted dry, pin bones removed

instructions: Heat the oven to 400°F and line a sheet pan with parchment paper.

Put the Brussels sprouts and sweet potato on the pan, drizzle with the oil, and season with 1 teaspoon of the salt, the pepper and the paprika. Toss, spread into an even layer, and bake for 20 minutes.
Meanwhile, mix the softened butter, garlic, chipotles, honey, lime zest, lime juice and cilantro in a small bowl until well combined.
After 20 minutes, take the vegetables out, add 2 tablespoons of the chipotle-honey butter, and toss to coat. Push the vegetables to the edges to make room in the center.
Put the salmon fillets in the center. Spread the remaining chipotle-honey butter over the tops and sprinkle with the remaining 1 teaspoon salt.
Bake until the salmon is cooked through and flakes easily with a fork, about 12 minutes. Divide the fish among four plates with the vegetables, garnish with cilantro, and serve with lime wedges.

Leftovers keep up to 3 days in the fridge. Reheat on a sheet pan in a 325°F oven for 10 to 12 minutes, in the air fryer at 350°F for 4 to 6 minutes, or in the microwave in 1-minute bursts, tossing the vegetables after each. From your cookbook, Everyday Eats, page 218.

recipes.name: Perfect Oven-Roasted or Slow Cooker Pot Roast

ingredients.name: Kosher salt
ingredients.prep: 2 tsp on the roast, ½ tsp with the vegetables

ingredients.name: Black pepper
ingredients.prep: freshly ground: 1 tsp on the roast, ½ tsp with the vegetables

ingredients.name: Yellow onion
ingredients.prep: large, halved and sliced into ¼-inch-wide strips

ingredients.name: Fresh thyme
ingredients.prep: 1 tsp roughly chopped leaves, plus more for serving

instructions: Oven method: heat the oven to 275°F. Season the roast generously with 2 teaspoons of the salt and 1 teaspoon of the pepper, then sprinkle with the flour and rub it in so the roast is evenly coated.
Heat the oil in a large Dutch oven over medium-high. Sear the roast until golden brown on both sides, about 4 minutes per side. It doesn't need to be cooked through. Move it to a clean plate.
Lower the heat to medium and add the onion, carrots, celery, garlic and the remaining ½ teaspoon salt and ½ teaspoon pepper. Cook, stirring, until the onion begins to soften, about 4 minutes.

Stir in the mustard, tomato paste and paprika. Pour in the vinegar and cook, scraping up the browned bits, until it has reduced by half, about 2 minutes. Add the broth, bring to a boil, then lower to a gentle simmer (about medium-low).

Add the thyme and bay leaves, then nestle the roast and its juices into the center of the pot with the vegetables and arrange the potatoes all around it. Cover with a fitted lid, move to the oven, and roast until the beef is fall-apart tender, about 4 hours.

Slow cooker method: season and sear the roast the same way in a large skillet. Put the onion, carrots, celery, garlic, remaining salt and pepper, mustard, tomato paste, paprika, vinegar and broth in the slow cooker and stir. Set the roast on top with the thyme, bay leaves and potatoes around it. Cover and cook on low 8 to 10 hours, until fall-apart tender.

Let the roast cool about 10 minutes before serving so the sauce can settle. Discard the bay leaves, shred the meat into large chunks, and divide it with the vegetables among shallow bowls. Ladle the sauce over the top and finish with fresh thyme.
Leftovers keep up to 4 days in the fridge, or freeze with some of the cooking liquid for up to 3 months. From your cookbook, Everyday Eats, page 184 (Beef, Pork, and Lamb).

recipes.name: Cuban-Inspired Picadillo
instructions: Heat the oil in a large, deep skillet or 3.5-quart braiser with a lid over medium. Cook the onion, bell pepper and garlic, stirring, until softened, about 4 minutes.
Add the beef and cook, breaking it up, until cooked through and no longer pink, about 7 minutes. Drain off the excess fat and return the beef to the pan.
Add the salt, pepper, garlic powder, cumin, oregano, chili powder and bay leaves and cook, stirring, until the spices are toasted, about 2 minutes.

Pour in the wine (if using) and let it reduce by half, about 1 minute. Add the broth, tomato sauce, olives, capers and potato and stir. Bring to a rapid simmer, then lower to a gentle simmer (about medium-low).
Cover and cook, stirring now and then, until the potato is fork-tender, about 15 minutes. Discard the bay leaves.
Ladle the picadillo over rice with a side of plantain chips, garnish with cilantro, and top with hot sauce if you like.

Leftovers keep up to 3 days in the fridge, separate from the garnishes. Reheat in a skillet over medium heat or in the microwave in 1-minute bursts, stirring after each. From your cookbook, Everyday Eats, page 177 (Beef, Pork, and Lamb).

recipes.name: One-Pot Butternut Squash and Sausage Pasta

ingredients.name: Black pepper
ingredients.prep: freshly ground, plus more for garnish

ingredients.name: Fresh parsley
ingredients.prep: ½ cup chopped, optional for serving

instructions: Heat the oil in a large pot over medium. Cook the shallot and garlic until tender, about 2 minutes.
Add the sausage and sage and cook, breaking up the meat, until browned and cooked through, 5 to 6 minutes. Drain off all but about 2 tablespoons of the fat.

Add the pasta, wine, broth, squash puree, coconut milk, salt and pepper and stir. Bring to a gentle simmer, without boiling, and cook uncovered, stirring often, until the pasta is al dente and the liquid is absorbed and creamy, 13 to 15 minutes. The sauce looks too thin at first, but the starch from the pasta thickens it.
Take the pot off the heat and let it rest about 2 minutes, stirring now and then. Plate with black pepper and parsley, if you like.

Notes from the book: if you use canned pumpkin instead of butternut squash, it won't taste like pumpkin pie. For gluten-free, use only brown rice pasta, because chickpea and other legume pastas won't release enough starch to thicken the sauce. From a cookbook page you photographed (the book's title and page number aren't visible in the photo).

recipes.name: One-Pot Green Curry Veggie Noodles

ingredients.name: Yellow onion
ingredients.prep: small (1 cup halved and thinly sliced)

ingredients.name: Thai green curry paste
ingredients.prep: the author uses Mae Ploy; use 1 tbsp if sensitive to heat, or red curry paste for milder

ingredients.name: Lime
ingredients.prep: 1 tbsp juice (about ½ lime), plus wedges for serving

ingredients.name: Cilantro
ingredients.prep: ¼ cup chopped leaves, plus more for serving

ingredients.name: Fresh Thai or regular basil
ingredients.prep: 2 tbsp thinly sliced leaves, plus more for serving

instructions: Heat the oil in a large, deep skillet over medium. Cook the onion, mushrooms, salt and pepper, stirring, until the onion begins to soften, about 3 minutes. Add the bok choy and cook another 2 minutes, until bright green and just beginning to soften.
Add the curry paste, toss to coat the vegetables, and toast until fragrant, about 1 minute.

While stirring, add the broth and coconut milk. Bring to a simmer, lower the heat to medium, and nestle in the ramen noodles. Cook 2 minutes undisturbed, flip the noodles, and cook 2 more minutes undisturbed. Keep cooking, tossing, until the sauce thickens and the noodles are tender and coated, about 2 more minutes. Take it off the heat.
Add the lime juice, cilantro and Thai basil and toss.

Divide between two bowls and top with the peanuts, green onions, more cilantro and Thai basil. Serve with lime wedges. Green curry paste tends toward the spicy side, which is why the book suggests 1 tablespoon if you're sensitive to heat. From a cookbook page you photographed (the book's title and page number aren't visible in the photo).

recipes.name: Sun-Dried Tomato, Pesto, and Mint Pasta

ingredients.name: Kosher salt
ingredients.prep: about 1 tbsp in the pasta water, ½ tsp in the skillet, plus more to taste

ingredients.name: Fusilli col buco
ingredients.prep: or brown rice linguine for gluten-free

ingredients.name: Black pepper
ingredients.prep: freshly ground, plus more to taste

ingredients.name: Basil pesto
ingredients.prep: store-bought, or the book's Lemon Basil Pesto

ingredients.name: Fresh mint
ingredients.prep: ¼ cup roughly chopped leaves, plus more for serving

ingredients.name: Parmesan
ingredients.prep: grated, for serving (omit for dairy-free); the book gives no amount, so ¼ cup is my estimate

instructions: Bring a large pot of water to a boil. Add a heavy pinch of salt (about 1 tablespoon) and the pasta and cook until al dente, following the package.

Meanwhile, heat 2 tablespoons of the oil from the sun-dried tomato jar in a large, deep skillet over medium. Cook the shallot, pepper flakes, garlic, zucchini, ½ teaspoon salt and the black pepper, stirring, until the zucchini is tender and slightly golden, 4 to 5 minutes. Add the sun-dried tomatoes and cook 2 more minutes.

instructions: Bring a large pot of water to a boil. Add plenty of salt (about 1 tablespoon) and the pasta and cook until al dente, following the package.

Lower the heat to medium-low. Add the remaining tablespoon of oil, the garlic, shallot, ½ teaspoon salt and the pepper flakes and cook, stirring, until the shallot has softened, about 2 minutes.

Add the wine and cook, stirring, until it has reduced by half, 1 to 2 minutes. Whisk in the mustard until emulsified, then add the coconut milk, tarragon, ½ teaspoon salt and the black pepper and whisk until smooth.

Save 1 cup of the starchy pasta water, then drain the pasta. Raise the heat to medium and add the pasta and kielbasa (and any juices from the plate) and toss to coat. Stir in ¼ cup of the pasta water, then add the baby kale 1 cup at a time, tossing until wilted and well distributed. instructions: Bring a large pot of water to a boil for the noodles.
Sauce: whisk the garlic, ginger, coconut aminos, coconut sugar, vinegar, lime juice, sesame oil, fish sauce and pepper flakes in a small bowl. Set aside.
Beef: in a large bowl, toss the sliced steak with the salt, pepper, tapioca flour and 1 tablespoon avocado oil until evenly coated. Set aside.

Noodles: when the water boils, add plenty of salt (about 1 tablespoon) and the noodles and cook until tender, about 3 minutes or as the package says. Save ½ cup of the starchy pasta water, drain the noodles, rinse them under cold water, and set aside.

To finish: heat 2 tablespoons avocado oil in a large, deep skillet over medium-high. Cook the steak in a single layer until golden brown on all sides and cooked through, 2 to 3 minutes per side. Move it to a clean plate.

Add the broccoli to the same skillet (with another tablespoon of oil if it looks dry) and cook, tossing, until slightly tender, 2 to 3 minutes. Add ¼ cup of the saved pasta water and let the broccoli steam uncovered until bright green and the liquid has evaporated, about 2 more minutes.

Lower the heat to medium and add the green onions, drained noodles, and beef with any juices. Toss to combine, then pour in the sauce and the remaining pasta water and toss constantly until the noodles are coated and the sauce starts to thicken, about 2 more minutes.
